articles.title: 2026 NFL Win Totals: Over/Unders For All 32 Squads
articles.summary: Check out the win totals and Over/Under odds for all 32 teams heading into the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body: The wait is finally over. With the New England Patriots and the Seattle Seahawks kicking off the year in a Super Bowl rematch on Wednesday, the 2026 NFL season is finally here. The Denver Broncos, Patriots and Seahawks led the league with 14 wins last year, but oddsmakers aren't buying a sequel. Meanwhile, after acquiring the reigning Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett, along with bringing back their franchise leader in sacks, the Los Angeles Rams' win total has surged. So which teams are projected to win the most games this year? And which teams might fall short of their expected win totals? Arizona drafted RB Jeremiyah Love as an explosive weapon who could help improve the offense, but the defense remains a major concern. Combined with the NFL’s fourth-hardest schedule, it’s no surprise their win total is set very low. Atlanta Falcons Over 7.5: +120 (bet $10 to win $22 total)Under 7.5: -140 (bet $10 to win $17.14 total) What To Know: The Falcons won eight games in 2025 and closed the season on a four-game winning streak. Despite that momentum, Atlanta enters 2026 with a relatively low win total under new head coach Kevin Stefanski with Tua Tagovailoa slated to start at quarterback in Week 1. Baltimore Ravens Over 11.5: +115 (bet $10 to win $21.50 total)Under 11.5: -140 (bet $10 to win $17.14 total) What To Know: The Ravens won only eight games in 2025, but much of that was due to Lamar Jackson missing four games while also dealing with injuries for most of the season. After parting ways with John Harbaugh after 18 seasons, Baltimore hired Jesse Minter as its new head coach and made a major splash in free agency by signing Trey Hendrickson. After firing Sean McDermott this offseason, Buffalo promoted offensive coordinator Joe Brady to head coach while also trading for DJ Moore and signing Bradley Chubb. Carolina Panthers Over 7.5: +115 (bet $10 to win $21.50 total)Under 7.5: -136 (bet $10 to win $17.35 total) What To Know: The Panthers won the NFC South last season with just eight wins. Coming off its first playoff appearance since 2017, Carolina significantly upgraded its defense with the additions of Jaelan Phillips and Devin Lloyd. Chicago Bears Over 9.5: +105 (bet $10 to win $20.50 total)Under 9.5: -125 (bet $10 to win $18 total) What To Know: The Bears won 11 games and the NFC North in Ben Johnson's first season in Chicago, but they are set to face the NFL’s toughest schedule in 2026. That, combined with several key defensive departures and the unexpected retirement of center Drew Dalman, has lowered their win total entering the season. However, Cincinnati made several major additions this offseason, including Dexter Lawrence II and Boye Mafe, among other moves. Combining the roster additions with the third-easiest schedule in the league, the Bengals are expected to take a major step forward in 2026. However, Cleveland made several major changes this offseason, including hiring Todd Monken and upgrading an offensive line that struggled throughout last year. The Browns will start Deshaun Watson in Week 1 but will have a QB roster of Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel and rookie Taylen Green. Dallas Cowboys Over 9.5: +100 (bet $10 to win $20 total)Under 9.5: -120 (bet $10 to win $18.33 total) What To Know: The Cowboys won seven games last season, mostly because they had one of the NFL’s worst defenses. However, their offense remained elite, ranking fifth in the league with 27.7 points per game. Dallas addressed its biggest weakness this offseason by trading for Rashan Gary and drafting Caleb Downs, two additions that could dramatically improve the defense. Combined with an easier schedule, those moves are a major reason why the Cowboys are projected for a higher win total in 2026. The big question entering 2026 is whether Denver can replicate that same success in close games. Their win total signals they will take a step back despite acquiring Jaylen Waddle via trade. With Mahomes expected to play in Week 1 against the Broncos, Vegas expects the Chiefs to bounce back to championship-level contention in 2026. After spending $281.5 million on the very first day of free agency alone, Las Vegas should be much improved in 2026. Kirk Cousins will start at quarterback in Week 1 against the Dolphins. Both are expected to return in 2026, and Los Angeles also added Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator. Even with those major boosts, the Chargers’ win total is somehow lower entering the season. Los Angeles Rams Over 11.5: -125 (bet $10 to win $18 total)Under 10.5: +105 (bet $10 to win $20.59 total) What To Know: The Rams won 12 games last season, and if not for a few bad breaks and costly mistakes in their losses to Seattle, it could have been Los Angeles hoisting the Lombardi Trophy. The Rams' biggest weakness, the secondary, was addressed this offseason with the addition of Trent McDuffie via trade. And now, after trading for the best defensive player in football in Myles Garrett, and signing Aaron Donald, the Rams do not have a weakness. They are currently the current Super Bowl favorite at +500. Miami will look completely different this season following the departures of Mike McDaniel and Tua Tagovailoa, as they were major sellers this offseason, trading away both Jaylen Waddle and Minkah Fitzpatrick while also releasing Tyreek Hill and Bradley Chubb. Jeff Hafley and Malik Willis are now set to lead a new era in Miami. Minnesota also signed Kyler Murray to a veteran minimum contract. Murray was named the starter for Week 1 over the Packers, beating out J.J. McCarthy for the job. New England now has the sixth-toughest schedule entering 2026, which is a major reason why Vegas is projecting a drop in wins. However, the Patriots did go out and trade for A.J. Brown, which should be a huge boost for Drake Maye. With Shough expected to enter 2026 as the full-time starter, New Orleans’ win total has increased, especially with the team also facing the second-easiest schedule in the NFL. articles.title: Christian McCaffrey in line to play vs. Rams in Australia, but don't forget his surprise Week 1 inactive status two years ago
articles.summary: 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey is back at practice and appears in line to play Thursday night against the Rams in Australia. Even if we all still remember him...
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey is back at practice in Melbourne, and he would appear in line to play Thursday night against the Los Angeles Rams in the Week 1 opener in Australia.

Even if everyone remembers what happened two years ago.

Here's the latest we know on McCaffrey, who is listed with an undisclosed injury: He missed Monday's practice, then returned to the field Tuesday. He's officially designated as questionable for Thursday's game.

McCaffrey suffered "tightness" in what was believed to be his calf in early August, but the 49ers have been opaque — which is nothing new — on the specifics of his injury and his availability. He missed multiple weeks of practice in August and skipped all three preseason games before ramping up his activity level again later.

The 49ers have said they're also managing his workload following a 414-touch campaign in 2025, the most by an NFL player since 2014. McCaffrey later said the downtime was "part of the plan from the jump," and not a setback, indicating that he and the team wanted to maintain his freshness for the long season.

But as 49ers fans and fantasy football players well know, assuming McCaffrey is a surety to play before the inactive players are announced 90 minutes prior to kickoff could be a mistake.

Don't forget what happened in Week 1 of the 2024 season

Two years ago, just prior to Week 1 of the 2024 season, McCaffrey was in a strangely similar situation, missing most of camp and all of the preseason with what was first called a calf strain. Head coach Kyle Shanahan downplayed the injury, and 49ers general manager John Lynch said he expected McCaffrey to be "out there and ready to roll."

McCaffrey was listed as questionable for the Monday game against the New York Jets , logged two full practices that week and appeared good to go. The consensus was that he'd play. But the consensus, it turned out, was wrong.

On gameday, McCaffrey was a surprise inactive for the Monday nighter, to the dismay of many. Shanahan later blamed Achilles tendinitis, not just the calf itself, for McCaffrey missing the game, and the 49ers placed him on injured reserve a few days later. He missed the first eight games that season and didn't make his 2024 season debut until Week 10 vs. Tampa Bay.

There's no evidence that the same thing is playing out now, but it would be foolish to count on McCaffrey playing in Australia until we know for certain that it's happening.

The other two true running backs on the roster — Jordan James and third-round pick Kaelon Black — have zero regular-season carries between them. James ran the ball six times for 28 yards and caught one 7-yard pass in the Niners' 41-6 playoff loss to the Seahawks in January. The 49ers also have Sincere McCormick , who ran for 183 yards for the Raiders in 2024, on the practice squad.

articles.title: Mahomes Mountain Week 1: 'It's Go Time' As 4 Quarterbacks Are Left Off
articles.summary: Find out who has a claim for the top spot in Nick Wright's Week 1 Mahomes Mountain NFL quarterback rankings as 28 signal-callers are tiered ahead of the kickoff.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes' place atop FOX Sports' Nick Wright's NFL quarterback power rankings has been so consistent the segment adopted his name. Mahomes remained atop Wright's summit, and can remind people why he's the king of the mountain when he starts the Kansas City Chiefs' Week 1 game against the Denver Broncos, nine months after sustaining a season-ending torn ACL. But if he stumbles, a group of worthy quarterbacks will try to dethrone him with their Week 1 performances. As for the rest of the rankings, Wright cracked down from his preseason edition, cutting a group of 32 down to 28. "It's go time," Wright said. "It was the offseason, you know, hopes springs eternal… There's only spots for seven rows." Here's where each of those quarterbacks fell on Mahomes Mountain ahead of Week 1: Off The Mountain Geno SmithNew York Jets Tua TagovailoaAtlanta Falcons Jacoby BrissettArizona Cardinals Deshaun WatsonCleveland Browns Wright: "These four quarterbacks are not climbing the mountain. Geno… it makes me upset. Tua, who I don't think is long to be the starter. Jacoby, shout out for getting paid. DeShaun, who's not long to be the starter." "Of these guys, the most likely to make the mountain is Geno." 7th Row: ‘Fans Believe’ Cam WardTennessee Titans Tyler ShoughNew Orleans Saints Jaxson DartNew York Giants Wright: "Cam Ward, Tyler Shough, Jaxson Dart are in one category: "Young players. Fans believe in them." Bryce YoungCarolina Panthers Aaron RodgersPittsburgh Steelers Malik WillisMiami Dolphins Kirk CousinsLas Vegas Raiders Wright: "Bryce got to the playoffs, that's kind of the end of the good story. Aaron's turning 43. Malik Willis has no weapons at all. Kirk kind of keeping the seat warm for Fernando Mendoza." 6th Row: ‘Polarizing Players’ Bo NixDenver Broncos Jayden DanielsWashington Commanders Brock PurdySan Francisco 49ers C.J. StroudHouston Texans Kyler MurrayMinnesota Vikings Daniel JonesIndianapolis Colts Wright: "I would say these are polarizing players. All of them. "Bo Nix, more wins than any quarterback ever through two years. Good numbers, been in the playoffs both years. Jayden Daniels, awesome rookie season, injury-riddled second year. Brock Purdy, once-upon-a-time, mainstay of the show. Last couple years, couple injuries, little disappointing play. CJ Stroud, his star is, you know, dimmed a bit.I think the book is in on Kyler, but there's a lot of hype surrounding the Vikings this year. Daniel Jones, who was in the midst of what we thought was a career renaissance, then popped his achillies." 5th Row: ‘Teams Are Content’ Jalen HurtsPhiladelphia Eagles Jared GoffDetroit Lions Jordan LoveGreen Bay Packers Justin HerbertLos Angeles Chargers Baker MayfieldTampa Bay Buccaneers Wright: "If you wanted to say, ‘anyone of these guys is the most underrated quarterback in the league,’ make the argument… All of these guys on the mountain are outside of the top 10, you can make a case for anyone of them to in the top 10, or a strong case against it. "My feeling on these guys is simple, if they are your starting quarterback, you're content." 4th Row: ‘Unquestionably, Great Resumes’ Joe BurrowCincinnati Bengals Dak PrescottDallas Cowboys Trevor LawrenceJacksonville Jaguars Sam DarnoldSeattle Seahawks Wright: "Four guys with pretty, unquestionably, great resumes. "Joe Burrow throws as pretty of a ball as anybody in the league. One of two active quarterbacks to beat Mahomes in the playoffs… Dak Prescott, if he's healthy, they have an elite offense. If he's healthy, he produces… The Prince (Trevor Lawrence) in Year 2 with Liam Coen with more from Travis Hunter, with more from Parker Washington, coming off his best individual season, and a great playoff game, even though he lost it. "Sam Darnold, back-to-back 4,000 yard seasons. The defending Super Bowl champion for one of the Super Bowl favorites." 3rd Row: ‘Could Win MVP’ Drake MayeNew England Patriots Caleb WilliamsChicago Bears Lamar JacksonBaltimore Ravens Wright: "Two young guys and one veteran, any of whom could win MVP this year." "Drake Maye absolutely could win MVP this year. It's not a bold prediction to say Drake could win MVP this year, even though he's not my pick. Caleb, I think has a very good chance at MVP this year because I think they're going to have to score a lot of points. Lamar, basically every year is an MVP favorite." 2nd Row: ‘Missed The Moment’ To Dethrone Mahomes Josh AllenBuffalo Bills Matthew StaffordLos Angeles Rams Wright: "The defending league MVP, and the five-time offseason MVP, in Josh Allen. Arguably the two strongest arms in the league… Patrick is still atop because the guy's who could have taken… missed the moment." 1st Row: ‘The Best In the League’ Patrick MahomesKansas City Chiefs Wright: "I understand it's now a controversial opinion to say Mahomes is the best quarterback in the league… We've debated a bunch if the Chiefs are a playoff team or not, even having the fifth-best Super Bowl odds, is that too high. Is Patrick Mahomes, coming off a torn ACL, the only quarterback on this mountain that, with that exact Chiefs roster, with that exact supporting case, we would be talking about at all as a legitimate Super Bowl threat. I would argue, yes."

articles.title: Week 1 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Should the Texans be favored vs. Buffalo?
articles.summary: The Texans defense had a huge game against Josh Allen last season.
articles.body:
Any good NFL defense has some level of physicality to it. Not many are as violent as the Houston Texans , however.

Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen knows this well. He was sacked a career-high eight times in a 23-19 loss to the Texans last season. It's rare to see Allen not in control, but it was the Texans defense that took over that game.

The Texans have a championship-level defense. There are stars at every level of it. They want to hit the opponent often and make it hurt. But defense doesn't sell as easily as a good offense, especially one with an elite quarterback. That is a reason the Bills are favored by a point in a great Week 1 matchup.

It's hard for people to pick the team with C.J. Stroud at quarterback over Allen's team. But the pendulum has swung too far on Stroud after a truly awful playoff performance against the Patriots . Last season he was 12th in adjusted EPA ( expected points added ) per play, 15th in success rate and the Texans were 18th in passer rating. That's not great but it's not at a Deshaun Watson level either. He's middle of the road. And with a defense that has a legitimate claim as the best in the NFL, average QB play is good enough to win a lot of games.

The Bills are my pick to win the AFC, but this is a tough matchup for them (and also, it wouldn't surprise me if the Texans are like the 2015 Broncos and ride a great defense to the Super Bowl). The pick is the Texans +1 . Either way, this is a really fun matchup for the opener. Unless you're the Bills offense, which has to face a scary and fierce Texans defense to start the season.

Here are the picks against the spread for Week 1 of the NFL season:

Hate to be square to start the season, but why aren't the Seahawks a bigger favorite? Seattle pounded New England on a neutral field in the Super Bowl, easily covering a 4.5-point spread, and now the spread is shorter? The Patriots should be better, though being without running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) won't help things. The Seahawks did lose some pieces (don't underrate the loss of offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak). However, I still trust them in this spot.

Yes, this could be overthinking the Rams' travel decisions. By now we all know what's going on: The 49ers have been in Australia since last week to get acclimated to the 17-hour time difference. The Rams will land a day before kickoff, then leave right after the game. The Rams are a smart organization and they didn't make this decision without thinking it through. Still, it seems hard to believe the Rams will be at their best given an incredibly aggressive travel plan (though others think they'll be fine, as was included in an in-depth report from Yahoo Sports' Jeff Eisenberg ). They did something similar for a trip to London and it worked with a 35-7 win over the Jaguars, but this seems like a much different challenge. Taking the points seems like the right move given this is a strange setting for an NFL game. The news that Aaron Donald won't play in the opener isn't too surprising and doesn't change much, though it's another positive for the 49ers.

Both teams were awful last season and the Titans — Cam Ward in particular — were uninspiring in the preseason. But here's a pick for the better coaching staff. I trust Robert Saleh to have his team ready. And I'll trust the beat reporters who say Ward looked much better in practices than he showed in preseason games.

It's rare I'll have a breakdown this basic: The Bears are getting an unbelievable 93% of the bets on the spread at BetMGM . I'm not very high on the Panthers this season and we know their injury issues. But I will not take a road favorite getting 93% of the bets. That's a promise.

This should be a fun one. Here's the test for the Saints, who were good in the second half last season but didn't really beat anyone either. The Lions have holes in the secondary that the Saints should be able to exploit. A touchdown spread seems like too much.

The Ravens' respect makes sense. We have kind of forgotten how good Lamar Jackson is. But what about forgetting how good the Colts were last season before Daniel Jones ' injury? There's some trepidation about taking the Colts in Jones' first game action since tearing his Achilles, though practice reports say he looks good. Also, new coach Jesse Minter was a good hire, but are we sure his defensive scheme will take hold immediately? The Colts are the biggest home underdog in Week 1 and that doesn't seem right.

The Steelers are old, but that might not catch up to them until later in the season. Meanwhile, the Falcons are starting Tua Tagovailoa after a concerning preseason. If the Steelers don't cover in this nearly perfect Week 1 setup, it might be a long season.

Let's roll out two stats. In each of Todd Bowles' four seasons as Buccaneers head coach, Tampa Bay has started 2-0. Meanwhile, the Bengals have been notorious slow starters under Zac Taylor. The Bengals have not escaped September with fewer than two losses since 2021. That all seems relevant to a sneaky fun Week 1 matchup.

It's not comfortable to pick the Browns, who are starting Deshaun Watson for some reason. But it is a talented team around the quarterback position. The Jaguars were very good last season and could easily cover, but weird things always happen in Week 1.

We'll see if the Commanders fixed their defensive issues. Working in their favor is this is Philadelphia 's first game under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. We're going to see Jalen Hurts under center more than we're used to. There could be a transition period, especially as the Eagles learn to play without A.J. Brown .

The brave among us will be picking the Raiders in survival pools this week. I don't think oddsmakers have fully accounted for how bad the Dolphins might be this season, even against a Raiders team that earned the first pick of the 2026 NFL Draft.

While there's some discrepancy on official closing lines, Stathead says the Chargers could be the first double-digit favorite in Week 1 since 2012 . (Some books have already moved the Chargers down to -9.5.) You just don't see an opening week spread this large very often. The Cardinals will not be good, but they can put up points. They're a backdoor cover threat in every game.

The Packers were favored in this game but the lines have shifted, and rightfully so. The Vikings were 9-8 last season with J.J. McCarthy at quarterback. Kyler Murray is what he is, but that's a lot better than McCarthy.

Let's keep this simple: If the Cowboys can't cover here, all that preseason buzz will go right out the window. It's only Week 1 but everyone is ready to dunk on those who were hyping up the Cowboys all offseason.

The most worn out line of the offseason was that the Broncos will regress. No kidding. They were 14-3. Only nine teams in NFL history have won 15 or more regular-season games. But the regression police have gone overboard. The Broncos are still a good team, just not one that will duplicate 14-3. Patrick Mahomes is in his first game back from a torn ACL and he's used to playing in the preseason. He didn't this year as he recovered. It wouldn't be that surprising to see Mahomes start a bit slowly, especially going up against one of the NFL's best defenses.

articles.title: How Aaron Rodgers can defy father time by learning from Tom Brady, Peyton Manning and other NFL legends
articles.summary: NFL News: Aaron Rodgers is 42, coming off a modest first season in Pittsburgh, and has publicly declared 2026-27 his final NFL ride. The Steelers went 3,322 pas.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers is 42, coming off a modest first season in Pittsburgh, and has publicly declared 2026-27 his final NFL ride. The Steelers went 3,322 passing yards and an AFC North title last year, but that ugly 30-6 playoff loss to Houston told a sharper story. Rodgers completed barely half his passes, finished with a 50.8 passer rating, and looked every bit his age under pressure. Now, with Mike McCarthy back on the sideline and a full training camp under his belt, the question is not whether Rodgers can survive the season. It is whether he can actually matter in it.Can Aaron Rodgers have one more elite season at 42?McCarthy, who coached Rodgers through his best years in Green Bay, has been openly enthusiastic about what he has seen this summer. "His mind's incredibly sharp," McCarthy told FOX Sports' Ralph Vacchiano. "But I'll be honest with you, his ball play in this camp has been top-notch. Obviously, I've coached a lot of football with him, but his ability to place the football... I'm not saying he lost any velocity on the ball, but if he has, it's definitely made up for with his anticipation. So he's getting the ball where it needs to be, on time. He's having a hell of a camp."Training camp praise is easy to find in August. Every team sounds good in July. But the McCarthy-Rodgers reunion is not nothing. Familiarity with a quarterback's rhythms and tendencies matters more when that quarterback is running on instinct and experience rather than raw arm talent. Rodgers said as much when explaining why he came back: "When the decision was made to hire Mike, I started opening my mind back up to coming back."The 2026 season will either be a fitting farewell or a cautionary tale. History gives us a map for both outcomes.What can Aaron Rodgers learn from Peyton Manning's final season?Manning's last year with the Broncos in 2015 is the most instructive parallel here. His arm was shot. His yards per attempt fell to 6.8, down from 8.3 during his 2013 MVP peak. Denver's coaching staff even benched him briefly in favor of Brock Osweiler. Manning eventually got his job back for the playoffs and won the Super Bowl, but he did it by throwing 179 passing yards per game in three postseason games and just two touchdown passes.What Manning did exceptionally well was not turning the ball over. One interception in three playoff games. He essentially handed the keys to Denver's suffocating defense and let Von Miller do the heavy lifting.The lesson for Rodgers is clear. Pittsburgh already has one of the NFL's most feared pass-rushing units. The skill position group around him has enough potential. Rodgers does not need to carry this team. He needs to manage the game, make sharp decisions, and stay out of his own way. That is a harder adjustment mentally than physically for a four-time MVP who has spent two decades trusting his arm to bail him out.What does Tom Brady's final season warn Aaron Rodgers about?Brady's 2022 swan song is probably the most uncomfortable cautionary tale for Rodgers. The Buccaneers lost Rob Gronkowski to retirement, their offensive line collapsed through injuries, and Tampa Bay limped to an 8-9 record before getting blown out by Dallas 31-14 in the Wild Card round. Brady was clearly diminished, operating behind a patchwork line and without the safety net of his most reliable target.Rodgers faces a similar offensive line concern. ESPN ranked Pittsburgh's line 30th in the league heading into this season. Pro Football Network had them third. That gap in assessment tells you everything about the uncertainty. If those blockers cannot hold up, Rodgers will be taking hits and making decisions under pressure he cannot afford at this stage of his career.The other lesson from Brady is simpler: when it is time, it is time. Brady came back from retirement for one more year and left on a losing note. Rodgers has already said this is it. Sticking to that decision, regardless of how this season goes, may be the smartest thing he does.How does Aaron Rodgers' career compare to Brett Favre's final years?The Favre connection is impossible to ignore. They both left Green Bay on complicated terms. They both played for the Jets and struggled there. Favre found his footing with the Vikings in 2009, throwing 33 touchdowns and just 7 interceptions to take Minnesota to the NFC Championship Game. Sound familiar?But Favre's 2010 follow-up was rough. Eleven touchdowns, 19 interceptions, and a 3-7 start that cost head coach Brad Childress his job. One strong season did not carry over to the next. Rodgers had something similar in Pittsburgh last year. Decent numbers, a division title, and then a playoff implosion. That reset button does not automatically carry over.Getting off to a fast start matters enormously. The Steelers open with the Falcons at home, then visit the Patriots, host the Bengals, and travel to Cleveland. There is no excuse for anything worse than 2-2 through that stretch. A slow start in 2026 could spiral in a way that even McCarthy cannot coach his way out of.What can Aaron Rodgers learn from Joe Montana's farewell season?Montana is the model Rodgers should actually be chasing. After San Francisco traded him to Kansas City in 1993, Joe Cool spent two seasons with the Chiefs and went out competing against the best of his generation. In 1994, he beat Steve Young and the 49ers head-to-head, threw for 203 yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions. Later that October, against John Elway on Monday Night Football, he drove 75 yards in the final seconds to win the game. That was his last NFL season.Rodgers flashed something similar in Week 1 last year, picking apart his former Jets team for 244 yards, four touchdowns, and no interceptions in a 34-32 win. Those moments exist in him. The question is whether he can find them consistently, and more critically, in January when it counts.Montana proved you can go out swinging even when the best years are behind you. Rodgers has enough left to do the same. But that requires discipline, self-awareness, and knowing his role within this offense. Not every play needs to be a highlight. Sometimes winning quietly is the sharpest thing a quarterback can do.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Believes Steelers Can Contend for Super Bowl 61 Title, 'I Believe in the Guys'
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers says he chose to join the Pittsburgh Steelers for what he expects to be his final NFL season because he believes his team can contend for a Super Bowl.
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers says he chose to join the Pittsburgh Steelers for what he expects to be his final NFL season because he believes his team can contend for a Super Bowl.

When asked Tuesday by Mad Dog Sports Radio's Adam Schein if he felt the Steelers were title contenders, Rodgers answered, "Yeah, of course. That's why I came back, because I believe in the guys."

NFL head coaching legend has a Minecraft hobby just as impressive

Rodgers went on to detail changes to the Steelers defense as a reason to believe in the team as a contender this season.

Changes noted by Rodgers included bringing in Jaquan Brisker, Jamel Dean and Sebastian Joseph-Day to join returners like T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith and Nick Herbig.

Rodgers added he felt the Steelers' defensive line has become "one of the bigger I've been a part of" as second-year players Derrick Harmon and Yahya Black prepare to join Cam Heyward.

"I feel like the AFC is very deep. Even in our own division, there's a number of teams with Super Bowl aspirations, which is great," Rodgers said.

The Steelers will get their first chance to work toward snapping the franchise's decade-long playoff streak when head coach Mike McCarthy makes his Pittsburgh debut in Sunday's Week 1 matchup against Tua Tagovailoa and the visiting Atlanta Falcons.

Pittsburgh won't begin division play until Week 3, when Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals come to town Sunday, Sept. 27.

articles.title: NFL 2026 predictions: Super Bowl, MVP, offensive and defensive player of the year, best offseason addition and more
articles.summary: Who will win Super Bowl 61 at SoFi Stadium in February 2027? The 2026 NFL season gets under way this week as defending champions Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots in a Super Bowl rematch at 1.20am BST on Thursday, live on Sky Sports NFL
articles.body:
NDAMUKONG SUH: Caleb Williams, QB, Chicago Bears. Caleb is set up for a lights-out year. Heading into his third season, he's going to step up, play lights-out football, and really do his thing.

NEIL REYNOLDS: Lamar Jackson, QB, Baltimore Ravens. Lamar is going to be healthy and rejuvenated under Jesse Minter.

BRIDGET CONDON: Joe Burrow, QB, Cincinnati Benglas. Joe Burrow has already shown us what he's capable of. Now his defense will finally be mediocre enough to give him his flowers. Burrow stays healthy and dominates his way back into the Super Bowl.

JASON BELL: Dak Prescott, QB, Dallas Cowboys. Dak will lead what could be the best offense in football as he feeds CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.

JEFF REINEBOLD: Josh Allen, QB, Buffalo Bills. He's the best player in the league with a better supporting cast and now in Joe Brady an offensive-minded head coach.

CAM HOGWOOD: Joe Burrow, QB, Cincinnati Bengals. When I heard Joe Burrow's 'this is it' speech demanding urgency from his Bengals this offseason, I really believed him. Injuries have hindered him over the last three seasons, so too has a below-par defense hamstringing their chances of contending for a Super Bowl. But a healthy Joe Burrow, with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins at his disposal, is capable of torching any defense in football.

NDAMUKONG SUH: Jahmyr Gibbs, RB, Detroit Lions . Jahmyr is going to be the focal point for Detroit - the true number-one option on that offense. As long as he stays healthy, he's going to put up elite, top-tier numbers.

NEIL REYNOLDS: Puka Nacua, WR, Los Angeles Rams. The Rams are going to unleash the NFL's best passing attack in 2026 and despite some off-field issues during this past offseason, there is no reason to believe that Puka Nacua's excellent level of play is going to drop off this season.

BRIDGET CONDON: Ja'Marr Chase, WR, Cincinnati Bengals. Burrow is going to need some help. This offense is going to explode this season. The better Joe does, the better Ja'Marr plays.

JASON BELL: Jahmyr Gibbs, RB, Detroit Lions. The Lions are going to find a way to feed him the ball and make sure he gets explosive plays.

JEFF REINEBOLD: Ja'Marr Chase, WR, Cincinnati Bengals. I've got a good feeling about the Bengals this season and Chase is a big reason why. With Zac Taylor dialling it up for Joe Burrow, Chase and co., the Bengals should be dynamic.

CAM HOGWOOD: Bijan Robinson, RB, Atlanta Falcons. When I look at the uncertainty around Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr at quarterback in Atlanta, it's hard not to feel like the entire Falcons operation rests on the shoulders of Bijan Robinson. He led the league in scrimmage yards last season and will deliver another huge return while spearheading Kevin Stefanski's offense.

NDAMUKONG SUH: Maxx Crosby, EDGE, Las Vegas Raiders. Maxx Crosby is coming back with a vengeance this year. He's heard all the outside noise and hype, and he's out to remind everyone who he is. He's an elite game-disrupter who just needed a quick chance to reset.

NEIL REYNOLDS: Myles Garrett, EDGE, Los Angeles Rams. The two-time Defensive Player of the Year was a wrecking ball in Cleveland last term and that was with the Browns holding very few leads where he could pin his ears back and attack. Teaming up with Aaron Donald, Garrett can complete the DPOY hat-trick.

BRIDGET CONDON: Aaron Donald, DE, Los Angeles Rams. It will be something out of a movie, retirement to DPOY. Aaron Donald will look everything like himself and more. People will be clawing to find out his retirement workout routine because he's coming back faster, stronger and even more dominant.

JASON BELL: Myles Garrett, EDGE, Los Angeles Rams. With the Rams' offense, Myles Garrett is finally going to be able to close out games rushing the passer.

JEFF REINEBOLD: Myles Garrett, EDGE, Los Angeles Rams. You aren't in Cleveland anymore, Myles! Teams are going to have to throw to keep up, which translates to more sack opportunities. Trent McDuffie and a guy named Aaron Donald will make him even better.

CAM HOGWOOD: Will Anderson Jr, DE, Houston Texans. There was a great quote from Texans defensive tackle Sheldon Rankins this offseason explaining how Anderson has reached a stage where he now realises his ability to "shut down practice" at any chosen moment, such has become of his dominance. I think we see that translate to live action games this Sunday. He established himself among football's game-changing disruptors last season while leading one of the most frightening defenses in the league. Myles Garrett will take some beating, but I think Anderson can be the man to pip him.

NDAMUKONG SUH: Mike McDaniel, offensive coordinator, Los Angeles Chargers. Mike McDaniel moving back into his absolute sweet spot as an offensive coordinator is huge. He has a phenomenal young talent in Justin Herbert, and McDaniel is going to take full advantage of dialing up creative schemes for him.

NEIL REYNOLDS: Jesse Minter, head coach, Baltimore Ravens. This is not meant to be disparaging to John Harbaugh, who was an excellent, Super Bowl-winning head coach during his 18 seasons in Baltimore. But a fresh start is probably best for everyone and I think Minter is going to improve the D and unleash a rejuvenated Lamar Jackson on the rest of the NFL.

BRIDGET CONDON: John Harbaugh, head coach, New York Giants. Harbaugh will lead the Giants to the NFC East title. He's just what New York needs to find their composure. Jaxson Dart isn't just an Abercrombie model - he's the next big thing. His time isn't this year but he's putting everyone on notice. He's coming.

JASON BELL: Myles Garrett, EDGE, Los Angeles Rams. The same reason why he will win Defensive Player of the Year!

JEFF REINEBOLD: Jeremiyah Love, RB, Arizona Cardinals. We saw signs of how special he can be in preseason, but he's got to stay healthy behind an offensive line that is a work in progress.

CAM HOGWOOD: Sean Mannion, offensive coordinator, Philadelphia Eagles. The Eagles may have won their division last season, but all was not well within one of the league's most uninspiring offenses, which endured something of an identity crisis under Kevin Patullo. His departure in the offseason prompted the appointment of former Green Bay Packers offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, who I think unlocks the best of Jalen Hurts with an exciting and revamped scheme on his way to head coaching contention.

NDAMUKONG SUH: The Minnesota Vikings win the NFC North. Everyone is hyped up on Detroit and Green Bay right now, but people are completely sleeping on Minnesota. They've got a fantastic head coach and great structure - they're the true dark horse in that division.

NEIL REYNOLDS: The Miami Dolphins take themselves out of the No.1 Draft pick stakes for 2027. The Dolphins have the youngest and arguably the worst roster in the NFL. But I think Malik Willis can produce just enough magic - to the dismay of ownership - to eliminate Miami from having the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, a position that could allow them to select their franchise quarterback of the future.

BRIDGET CONDON: The Tennessee Titans defense is going to be a lot better than people think. Robert Saleh has been part of nine top-10 defenses, and in his nine seasons as either a defensive coordinator or head coach, his teams finished top five in total defense five times. Saleh isn't going to let the Titans stay a joke.

JASON BELL: The Dallas Cowboys. Dak Prescott and co. will be in the Super Bowl conversation all year long.

JEFF REINEBOLD: The Cincinnati Bengals win the AFC North. Just a few stops a game and a turnover or two is all that is required, because the Bengals can score with any team in the league.

CAM HOGWOOD: From an individual perspective, Dallas Turner, while perhaps not a surprise to Vikings fans, is a name to keep an eye on. I think the third-year linebacker is a strong bet to establish himself among the leading pass rushers in the league and the face of Brian Flores' Minnesota Vikings defense following the departure of Jonathan Greenard. Here is his chance to break out as a complete and consistent threat up front to reach double figures in sacks. I think the Vikings as a whole could surprise some people and return to the playoffs behind a reinvigorated Kyler Murray.

NDAMUKONG SUH: The Los Angeles Chargers make the AFC Championship. The Chargers have every piece in place between their offensive coaching staff, Justin Herbert, and a tough defense. With Khalil Mack playing at an elite level, they're going to gel as a complete collective unit when it matters most.

NEIL REYNOLDS: The Rams struggle out of the gate. Despite a Week 1 win over the San Francisco 49ers, the Rams will follow their Australian adventure by losing three of their next four to Denver, Philadelphia and Buffalo. The biggest issues will be Davante Adams' swollen ankle after he gets bitten by a spider while Down Under and the confusing fact that Matthew Stafford picks up an Aussie accent he cannot shake until mid-October. The Rams will ride out their rough patch and still win the Super Bowl.

BRIDGET CONDON: The Steelers will have their first losing season since 2003 - Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy are going to show us why you never go back to your ex. It seems good in the moment, you remember all the good times you had. But... there was a reason you broke up. It wasn't working and it still wont work. The experiment will blow up by midseason. We'll be talking about a lot more than Bougnettes when the Saints upset the Steelers in Paris.

JEFF REINEBOLD: CJ Stroud bounces back and leads the Houston Texans to the AFC Championship Game. They have the best defense in a weak division and the stage is set for Stroud to get back to his former self.

CAM HOGWOOD: The New Orleans Saints win the NFC South and reach the playoffs for the first time since 2020 behind Tyler Shough, who proves to be Kellen Moore's answer at quarterback.

NDAMUKONG SUH: Denver Broncos to beat Chicago Bears. Denver takes it all home. Bo Nix is my pick for Comeback Player of the Year, and I have immense faith in a head coach like Sean Payton. He's already taken an elite group to the conference championship, and once Sean gets back to the Super Bowl stage, he's simply not losing it.

NEIL REYNOLDS: Los Angeles Rams to beat Baltimore Ravens. This could be a quarterback-led shootout with Matthew Stafford and Lamar Jackson trading blows. But those defensive closers in LA - Garrett and Donald - will ultimately make the difference in LA.

BRIDGET CONDON: Cincinnati Bengals to beat the Los Angeles Rams. The Rams have it all - the coach, the quarterback, the defensive duo, the home-field Super Bowl advantage. It's too perfect! Life isn't a storybook ending so the Bengals are going to get their revenge. The Rams will score with time expiring in the fourth to make it 34-35. Sean McVay will try to go for two but Puka Nacua will drop the pass in the corner of the endzone to make the Bengals winners of their first Super Bowl.

JASON BELL: Los Angeles Rams to beat Denver Broncos. The Super Bowl will be all about defense - Myles Garrett and the Rams take it.

JEFF REINEBOLD: Los Angeles Rams to beat Buffalo Bills. Two of the league's best quarterbacks duel it out in SoFi Stadium. The Rams have always scored points and now have three of the best players in the league on defense in Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald and Trent McDuffie. Add the best coach in the NFL and you get the best team in football.

CAM HOGWOOD: Cincinnati Bengals to beat Los Angeles Rams. I'm an enormous Joe Burrow believe. I think he and the Bengals beat Matthew Stafford in a straight shoot-out, avenging their loss from Super Bowl LVI.

articles.title: New J.J. McCarthy Rumors Reveal Why Vikings Decided Against Trade, Release Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Quarterback J.J. McCarthy's contract situation reportedly may have played a role in the Minnesota Vikings keeping him on the roster rather than releasing him.
articles.body:
Quarterback J.J. McCarthy's contract situation reportedly may have played a role in the Minnesota Vikings keeping him on the roster rather than releasing him.

According to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer, the Vikings would have been on the hook for the remaining $4.85 million in guarantees on McCarthy's contract had they cut him due to a collective bargaining agreement rule that prevents teams from renegotiating a drafted player's contract over their first three seasons.

Additionally, Pelissero noted that the Vikings had "no intention" of losing McCarthy for nothing, especially since he is "well-liked in the locker room and has gone 6-4 as a starter."

NFL head coaching legend has a Minecraft hobby just as impressive

Selected 10th overall by the Vikings in the 2024 NFL draft out of Michigan, McCarthy has had a rocky start to his NFL career.

He missed his entire rookie season due to a knee injury, and although he won the starting job entering the 2025 campaign, injuries limited him to only 10 starts.

McCarthy did go 6-4, but his production left plenty to be desired, as he completed 57.6 percent of his passes for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions, while also rushing for 181 yards and four scores.

Given McCarthy's inconsistent play, the Vikings decided to add some competition by signing longtime Arizona Cardinals starting quarterback Kyler Murray in free agency.

It wasn't long before Murray pulled ahead in the quarterback battle, and he was ultimately named the Vikings' QB1 last month.

Given the presence of Murray and veteran backup quarterback Carson Wentz on the roster, there was some speculation that the Vikes would look to cut or trade McCarthy prior to the start of the season.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler said Aug. 30 on SportsCenter that McCarthy's standing in Minnesota was a "question that looms around the league."

Despite that, the Vikings decided to keep McCarthy, and they currently have three quarterbacks on their 53-man roster, plus Max Brosmer on the practice squad.

There is a distinct possibility that McCarthy could open the regular season as the Vikings' QB3 behind Murray and Wentz, and if that is the case, it could suggest that Minnesota would be open to moving on from him in the right scenario, especially since 2027 is the final year of his contract.

articles.title: Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs Sounds Off on Being Consensus No. 1 Fantasy Football Pick in 2026
articles.summary: Detroit Lions star running back Jahmyr Gibbs is well aware that the hopes of many fantasy football managers are resting on him in 2026.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions star running back Jahmyr Gibbs is well aware that the hopes of many fantasy football managers are resting on him in 2026.

Gibbs—who has been widely considered the best option to go first overall in fantasy football drafts leading up to the start of the regular season—told Tim Twentyman of the Lions' official website that he "for sure" picked himself with the No. 1 overall selection in fantasy.

The 24-year-old, fourth-year running back added, "I'm either going to make a lot of people happy or mad."

NFL head coaching legend has a Minecraft hobby just as impressive

Gibbs was a great fantasy football pick each of his first three seasons, compiling 3,580 yards and 39 touchdowns on the ground, plus 181 receptions for 1,449 yards and another 10 scores.

He was named to the Pro Bowl each of those seasons, and he accomplished that despite sharing the backfield with David Montgomery.

Things will be different for Gibbs this season, though, as Montgomery was traded to the Houston Texans during the offseason, meaning Gibbs is now the undisputed RB1 in Detroit and fantasy football.

The Lions did sign former Kansas City Chiefs running back Isiah Pacheco as Gibbs' backup, but with Pacheco landing on injured reserve and missing at least the first four games of the season, there is no serious threat to Gibbs' workload for the first month of the campaign.

Given what Gibbs was able to do while playing 57 percent, 56 percent and 67 percent of the Lions' offensive snaps over his first three seasons, the idea of him playing closer to 80 percent of the snaps has fantasy football managers excited.

In Yahoo fantasy football leagues, Gibbs boasts an average draft position of 1.3, and Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson is the only other player in the same neighborhood at 2.1.

That means Gibbs has almost been a slam dunk pick for those selecting first overall, and fantasy football managers are banking on the idea that if they have the first pick, Gibbs gives them a massive advantage, much like superstar fantasy football running backs of the past like Marshall Faulk and LaDainian Tomlinson.

articles.title: Super Bowl 61 Betting Odds, Where Do Rams, Seahawks, Patriots Sit Among Top Favorites?
articles.summary: Hours before the 2026 NFL season kicks off, the latest odds for Super Bowl 61 have dropped with the Los Angeles Rams strongly favored to lift the Lombardi Trophy in February.
articles.body:
Hours before the 2026 NFL season kicks off, the latest odds for Super Bowl 61 have dropped with the Los Angeles Rams strongly favored to lift the Lombardi Trophy in February.

Per FanDuel Sportsbook , the Rams are a +550 favorite (bet $100 to win $550) to win the Super Bowl.

Here are the top-10 favorites to win Super Bowl 61 based on the betting odds.

It's not a surprise that the Rams are favored to win a championship after acquiring Myles Garrett and getting Aaron Donald out of retirement, but the extent to which they sit above every other team is remarkable.

One good sign for the Rams is they don't have lower odds because Yahoo Sports' Ben Fawkes noted preseason favorites at +500 or better have not won a Super Bowl in the last 30 years.

Since 2019, the only preseason favorite to win the Super Bowl were the Kansas City Chiefs in 2023.

Somewhat surprisingly, the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks are not second on the list. They are third because the Buffalo Bills are at No. 2 in the odds.

The Seahawks defeated the Rams in the NFC Championship Game last season before going on to beat the New England Patriots in Super Bow 60. Three games between the Seahawks and Rams during the 2025 were decided by a total of three points.

Despite the addition of A.J. Brown to their receiving corps, the reigning AFC champion Patriots only have the fifth-best odds in their own conference to win the Super Bowl. They are behind the Bills, Baltimore Ravens, Los Angeles Chargers and Chiefs.

The Chargers' odds are remarkable just given the history of the franchise, but it does speak to how much optimism there is around the offense with Mike McDaniel calling plays and Justin Herbert at quarterback.

Another surprise is that the Denver Broncos, who easily could have represented the AFC in the Super Bowl last season if Bo Nix had been healthy, are third in the odds just among AFC West teams.

It could be reasonably argued that Denver has the best roster on paper in the AFC. The Broncos were the No. 1 seed in the AFC last season with a 14-3 record and acquired Jaylen Waddle to play next to Courtland Sutton.

Just in case you are wondering about the low end of the totem pole, FanDuel has the Arizona Cardinals with the longest odds at +100000. The next four teams are the Miami Dolphins (+75000), New York Jets (+40000), Cleveland Browns (+40000) and Las Vegas Raiders (+15000).

We will find out how smart the oddsmakers are starting on Wednesday when the Patriots and Seahawks kickoff the season in a Super Bowl rematch at Lumen Field.

articles.title: 'Tush Push Tater' and New Concession Menu Items Unveiled for Eagles, Steelers, Browns, Chiefs & More
articles.summary: Football fans will have no shortage of specialty concessions as they attend NFL games this year.
articles.body:
Football fans will have no shortage of specialty concessions as they attend NFL games this year.

With the 2026 season ready to kick off, Aramark unveiled additions to menus at stadiums for the Pittsburgh Steelers, Cincinnati Bengals, Denver Broncos, Houston Texans, Minnesota Vikings, Kansas City Chiefs, Cleveland Browns and Philadelphia Eagles.

Among the headliners is a "Tush Push Tater" at Lincoln Financial Field. Referencing the Eagles' signature play, the dish is a deep-fried potato topped with a fried chicken cutlet, mac and cheese and hot honey jam.

NFL head coaching legend has a Minecraft hobby just as impressive

Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati will treat fans to a "Who Dey Sausage," a 24-inch BBQ cheddar pork sausage.

The Steelers are going a step further at Acrisure Stadium. The franchise is opening the 1933 Club , a membership-only space for season-ticket holders. Thankfully, you won't need any special privileges to enjoy the "Black N' Gold Chicken and Waffle" sandwich.

The waffles are dyed black and gold, and since this is Pittsburgh, there are sweet potato fries and coleslaw accompanying the fried chicken.

Over in the Mile High City, you may want to stop over before the game starts to try the "Beast in a Blanket." A two-foot hot dog is combined with burnt ends. Cheddar and goat cheese is weaved inside the puff pastry.

Getting that back to your seat will be no easy feat.

In terms of portability, the Browns' hot dog flight is a winner. One of the three mini all-beef dogs is covered with buffalo chicken dip. Another combines a hot dog with spaghetti and meatballs. The brisket dog, meanwhile, is pretty self-explanatory.

Burger aficionados will want to make their way to Arrowhead Stadium. The Chiefs are adding a lava burger, which is a cheese-stuffed burger with bacon, tomato, chives and a jalapeno popper.

The Texans are treating fans to a new meatball bao, a mac and cheese bowl with a Southern spin, and a fried chicken breast that's tossed in strawberry buffalo sauce.

A meatball sub is among the fresh offerings at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. The Vikings are also introducing the "Raid Burger," a double bacon cheeseburger with buffalo cheese curds and an onion ring.

articles.title: Tony Romo’s strange Cowboys story takes a surprising turn as Dan Campbell finally admits what really happened that night
articles.summary: NFL News: Dan Campbell has confirmed Tony Romo’s story about a strange prank from their Dallas Cowboys days, admitting he really did press a lit cigarette again.
articles.body: Dan Campbell has confirmed Tony Romo’s story about a strange prank from their Dallas Cowboys days, admitting he really did press a lit cigarette against the quarterback’s hand. Romo recently told Pardon My Take about the night, and Campbell later gave his own version on the St. Brown Podcast. The Detroit Lions coach said Romo was a young rookie, but added that he took some of the pain himself afterward.Dan Campbell confirms Tony Romo’s cigarette prankThe story goes back to 2003, when Campbell joined Dallas after spending his first four NFL seasons with the New York Giants. Romo was an undrafted rookie trying to find his place on the Cowboys, while Campbell was already an experienced tight end and respected player in the locker room.Romo recently remembered that night on Pardon My Take. He said Campbell was smoking when he called him over and suddenly put the cigarette against his hand. Romo recalled asking, “What are you doing?” before Campbell replied, “isn’t that funny?”Campbell has now confirmed that Romo’s memory was accurate. During the St. Brown Podcast, Amon-Ra St. Brown asked his Lions coach about the story, and Campbell did not try to deny it.“It’s a true story,” Campbell said. “Romo was a pup. I got there in 2003. He was a rookie free agent. And everybody liked Romo. I liked Romo. And so Romo went, ‘Hey man, where are you guys going tonight? What are you doing?’ And we go out one night. He’s over there talking to somebody. I don’t know what. So I’m like, ‘Hey, come here! I got something for you. And I put it (cigarette) out. I didn’t put it out. I put it on him. Just don’t ask me why. So, I gave him a little singe.’”Dan Campbell says Tony Romo did not tell the whole storyCampbell then added another detail that Romo had left out. He said he tried to make up for the prank by putting the cigarette out on his own hand too.“Just to make him feel better, he didn’t mention that I put it out in the palm of my hand after I did that,” Campbell added. “So, it’s not like he’s paying. I’m paying, too, alright. Now, he didn’t want to pay. He shouldn’t have had to pay.”The story has apparently been around for years. Dallas sportswriter Bob Sturm had previously discussed the incident with Campbell on his radio show. Campbell jokingly denied it then, saying, “He is talking about Dan Camel. Not Dan Campbell.”This time, Campbell openly admitted it and said it was not the only time he had pulled that kind of prank. When St. Brown asked if he had done it to other people, Campbell replied, “I’ve done that a couple of times.”Romo eventually became one of the Cowboys’ best quarterbacks of his era after entering the NFL as an undrafted free agent. articles.title: Browns news: Shedeur Sanders' Week 1 status after losing QB1 job to Deshaun Watson

articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns are just a few days away from kicking off their 2026 NFL season. Recently, head coach Todd Monken announced that veteran Deshaun Watson would be the team's starting quarterback, winning the job over rising second-year man Shedeur Sanders .

Recently, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reported that Monken "Said he anticipates Shedeur Sanders being the No. 2 QB on Sunday," on X, formerly Twitter.

It's certainly not off the table that Sanders could see some reps at quarterback for the Browns this year.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

For one, Watson is coming off a devastating injury he suffered during the 2024 season that caused him to miss all of last year, so it's unclear how well his body will hold up now that he is back in the NFL grind.

Furthermore, the Browns cycled through two quarterbacks last season– Joe Flacco and Dillon Gabriel –before Sanders finally got his turn as the team's starter. Although he didn't exactly blow away expectations when he reached that point, it still goes to show how quickly things can change from week to week in the NFL.

Not many fans expect the Browns to compete for much of anything except for a top draft pick this year, with the team having traded superstar Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams earlier this offseason.

However, if Sanders were to get another opportunity to play this year and showcase some improvement from last season, it would at least give the Browns some beacon of hope for the future.

Cleveland is set to kick off its season on Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars on the road.

articles.title: ClutchPoints' NFL Power Rankings, Week 1: Rams lead the way
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL season is finally here, and with it comes new expectations. Regardless of how your team performed last year, this season offers a new opportunit...
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season is finally here, and with it comes new expectations. Regardless of how your team performed last year, this season offers a new opportunity to exceed (or fall short of) expectations.

These Week 1 NFL Power Rankings will hopefully get you back into the football spirit (if you aren't already), as the first game of this year starts on Wednesday, a Super Bowl rematch between the Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots .

The Los Angeles Rams find themselves atop the Week 1 NFL Power Rankings, as their offseason was one of a team that expects to have a target on its back. With its trade for Myles Garrett and its coaxing of Aaron Donald out of retirement for one last hoorah, the Rams are positioning themselves to be the belle of the ball this season.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

An impending legal situation surrounding Puka Nacua could cloud the offense a bit if he is forced to miss time, but as long as Matthew Stafford reclaims his MVP form from last year, the Rams will be one of the best teams in the league.

Speaking of the NFC West, the Seahawks, who are the defending Super Bowl champions, surprisingly find themselves in second place in ClutchPoints' Week 1 NFL Power Rankings. To no fault of their own, as they were able to keep most of their core this offseason, Seattle will be in a tough fight to even win the division, as that is far from a guarantee.

A tough defense and the addition of Jaylen Waddle give the Denver Broncos an even better shot at winning the AFC, a year after coming up short in the AFC Championship Game. With Bo Nix fully recovered from a broken ankle, the offense will be looking to take a step forward as one of the most well-rounded teams in the entire NFL.

The Joe Brady era is looking to start off on the right foot, but a Week 1 matchup with the Houston Texans will give Brady and Josh Allen fits. However, the Bills are one of the best-built teams in the AFC, as their acquisition of DJ Moore this offseason finally gives Allen a proven WR1 option to lead the offense.

Question marks about what kind of team Brady will lead will be the biggest aspect to figure out this year, and as long as Brady's offense doesn't change too much of its identity, winning the AFC East and factoring into the race for the Super Bowl is in the cards.

The Patriots don't look to be the favorites in the AFC heading into the 2026 NFL season, even after representing the conference in last year's Super Bowl. Having acquired A.J. Brown this offseason to pair with Drake Maye , the Patriots' passing attack should take a step forward.

But outside of Brown, they didn't make a ton of improvements to the roster, and the lack of progress TreVeyon Henderson has shown will not help the offense take a big enough step forward to compete with other AFC rosters.

It was quite an impressive first season for Ben Johnson at the helm, as an 11-5 finish, an NFC North title, and a solid postseason performance showed that the Chicago Bears will be a threat for a long time. The trio of pass catchers ( Luther Burden III , Colston Loveland , and Rome Odunze) will help revitalize the CHI offense, helping Caleb Williams grow as he enters his third season.

Injury concerns have made it quite the uneven offseason for the San Francisco 49ers, as Christian McCaffrey , Nick Bosa , and Mike Evans have all been on the injury report during training camp. Positive signs from the 49ers about the availability of all three, including Bosa, mean they will hopefully be available in Week 1, as they will need all the help they can get against the Rams.

The Jacksonville Jaguars are hoping to put together another division-winning season in 2026, as Liam Coen was exactly what the JAX offense needed to take a big step forward. Trevor Lawrence and Parker Washington were on a different level to end the year last season, and the offense is in a position to once again be one of the best in the league this time around.

Jesse Minter and Declan Doyle are looking to help the Baltimore Ravens reclaim their spot as one of the best teams in the AFC, and this time they will be looking to do it on both sides of the ball. A healthy Lamar Jackson , paired with a revamped group of offensive weapons, will hopefully do the trick in a Ben Johnson-esque offense, and Minter, who was a coach on the BAL staff a few years back, will be looking to unlock a defensive unit that has the right pieces in place but just needs a bit better coaching to become one of the league's best units again.

It will be the Jordan Love show to begin the 2026 NFL season for the Green Bay Packers, as the ongoing legal situation surrounding Josh Jacobs has landed him on the Commissioner's Exempt List. Love and his quartet of pass catchers ( Christian Watson , Jayden Reed , Matthew Golden , Tucker Kraft ) will be tasked with leading this offense under Matt LaFleur, and with a tough NFC North slate ahead of them, it could be an MVP-caliber year for Love if all the pieces fall into place.

Everyone knows that the Houston defense is legit, but the development of C.J. Stroud as he enters his four season will be what makes — or breaks — the Texans' playoff hopes. Having made the playoffs last year, the Texans will once again look to ride star edge rusher Will Anderson back to the AFC postseason, but Stroud's play will be the biggest storyline to follow this year, especially with a shakeup in their WR room.

Mike McDaniel is going to LOVE having Justin Herbert as his quarterback, as the Los Angeles Chargers have very high expectations to meet this season. Playing in one of the toughest divisions in the league this year, McDaniel and Herbert will need to be on the same page, as an easy, early-season slate against the Cardinals and Raiders gives LAC a real shot to start 2-0.

The 2026 NFL season might be a make or break for the Philadelphia Eagles and Jalen Hurts , as they were not themselves last year. While a new offensive coordinator will have some kinks to iron out, this may be the change that Hurts and the offense needs, especially with DeVonta Smith taking over WR1 duties.

Expect the offense to refocus more on Saquon Barkley , likely taking a bit of the run game away from Hurts this year.

After missing the playoffs last year, the Detroit Lions have an easier schedule and a top offense in the league, a perfect pairing to factor into the NFC playoff race yet again. With Jahmyr Gibbs looking to go nuclear this year after signing a lucrative long-term deal, Detroit will need to put up a lot of points every week with how their defense (especially their secondary) looks right now.

The return of Patrick Mahomes will be a major boost to the Kansas City offense, as missing the playoffs last year gave the Chiefs a chance to do a much-needed reset. Needing to build around Mahomes on offense, signing Kenneth Walker III was exactly what this team needed — a superstar to anchor the offense early on in the year as Mahomes reacclimates to football.

You clearly can never count out Mahomes and the Chiefs, and even though they are in a very tough AFC West division, they absolutely should be in contention in the AFC playoff race.

It seems like the Dallas Cowboys always find themselves near the middle of the pack to start the year, and this year's Week 1 NFL Power Rankings is no different. While the offense is once again slated to be one of the league's best, an improved defense will need to step up if this roster wants to play a part in the NFC East divisional race.

This year is a year that the divisional race is open for any of the four teams to take, giving Dallas a fantastic chance to finally get back to the playoffs.

What version of Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals will we see this year? Will it be the record-setting offense that sees Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins , and Chase Brown form the best offense in the league, or will injuries catch up with Burrow yet again and stop this attack in its tracks?

With a lot up in the air for the AFC North, the Bengals have every chance to win the division — it just depends on the health of their franchise QB if that will happen or not.

The end of the 2025 NFL season was a promising one for the New Orleans Saints, as Tyler Shough took over as QB1 and formed a solid pairing with receiver Chris Olave . With both guys back for this year, the Saints are in line to be one of the most fun teams to watch this season.

With the NFC South continuously a toss-up, don't be surprised if New Orleans is in the race for the division down the stretch this year, as they have the talent on both sides of the ball, as well as with head coach Kellen Moore, to make that next big move.

Kyler Murray will be tasked with reclaiming the QB room in Minnesota, as the JJ McCarthy project looks to be dead in the water for Kevin O'Connell. As the Vikings look to factor into the race for the NFC North again, Murray will need to reclaim some of his early years with the Cardinals, as he and the tough Brian Flores-led defense will look to get the Vikings back to relevancy in 2026.

The swan song for Aaron Rodgers will include Mike McCarthy, as the former Packers QB and HC are paired up once again. There isn't a ton to be excited about with this Pittsburgh roster, as a lot of their talent is the same as what drove Mike Tomlin out of town this past offseason.

Adding McCarthy isn't a needle mover, as the old-school head coach will be tasked with keeping what Pittsburgh is known for here while also improving in the other areas. If Rodgers wants to make some noise in his last hurrah, he will need players like DK Metcalf , Michael Pittman Jr. , Jaylen Warren , and Rico Dowdle to pick up some slack this year.

A three-year extension for Baker Mayfield closes the book on one potential in-season distraction for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, as this team (that fell short of making the postseason in Week 18 last year) needs to try to correct the ship this year.

Todd Bowles is on a bit of a hot seat with how Tampa looked last season, although his steadying presence has been nice for a team in a bit of flux, something that will hopefully help them correct a few things this season.

The John Harbaugh era is underway for the New York Giants, giving this franchise its most to look forward to since the Eli Manning days. Pairing second-year Jaxson Dart with Matt Nagy definitely doesn't scream offensive output by any means, so that will need to be an aspect of this team that gets figured out sooner rather than later.

A healthy Daniel Jones is hopefully the missing piece for the Indianapolis Colts, as a fast start last year was stunted by Jones' season ending early. A heavy workload for Jonathan Taylor is likely in store again this season, which is great news for fantasy football teams, but there isn't a ton exciting about this Colts roster heading into the 2026 season, putting them near the bottom of the Week 1 NFL Power Rankings.

An NFC South divisional win, coupled with a strong showing in the playoffs, ended an impressive season for the Carolina Panthers, even though they hovered around .500 all season. However, Bryce Young and the Carolina offense need to take another step forward, and with their group of skill players staying the same, it remains to be seen where that improvement will come from.

It is a welcomed sight to have Jayden Daniels back playing football, as the NFL is better when he is on the field. Injuries ended his season early last year, and with it went the chances of the Washington Commanders. Fielding an old team around Daniels and head coach Dan Quinn, the 2026 season is a big deal for this franchise, as another poor, injury-riddled year could spell the end of the current coaching staff.

While Tua Tagovailoa won the Atlanta Falcons' QB1 job, it is not an encouraging sign that it took this long for the coaching staff to anoint him the starter. Needing a full offseason to see which southpaw was the best option does not give Kevin Stefanski a fighting chance in his first year as head coach, as the offense (outside of Bijan Robinson and Drake London ) will likely struggle yet again.

The Robert Saleh era is underway in Tennessee, and with it comes a renewed excitement for the future of this franchise. Getting Brian Daboll to help guide Cam Ward in his second year has his compass pointing up, and the defense should be much improved with Saleh's influence, giving the Titans a chance to sniff a .500 record this season.

The Fernando Mendoza era won't start in Week 1, as Kirk Cousins will be the starter to open the year, helping kick off Klint Kubiak's tenure in Las Vegas. The Raiders are facing an uphill battle this year with how tough the rest of the AFC West division is, so the 2026 NFL season will likely be a foundational year for Kubiak and the new roster.

Another rough year likely spells the end to Aaron Glenn's unfortunate tenure as the New York Jets head coach, but a revamped group of offensive weapons will give Geno Smith a chance. With Smith back in town for at least this year, the QB room is temporarily stable while the Jets yet again search for their QB of the future.

Todd Monken has his hands full in his first head-coaching gig, as the Cleveland Browns have decided to move forward without franchise icon Myles Garrett . With some talent on both sides of the ball but depth issues dominating headlines, it will be another tough year for a Browns roster that has yet to lock down its QB of the future.

Rookie wide receivers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion are two guys to root for on the offense, as they could finally be the pieces the Browns need to revamp their WR room.

Jeff Hafley and Malik Willis will have their hands full in their first season together in Miami, as the Dolphins are undergoing a complete reset. With three rookie wideouts (Chris Bell, Caleb Douglas, and Kevin Coleman) likely earning a majority of time at wide receiver, Willis will be tasked to handling the development of that trio.

For Willis, his dual-threat abilities will make the Miami offense fun to watch at times, but playing from behind often will make the 2026 NFL season a bit tough for the Dolphins, as they build their roster back up.

The team taking up the last spot in the Week 1 NFL Power Rankings is the Arizona Cardinals, as first-time head coach Mike LaFleur has his hands full. A recent extension to wide receiver Michael Wilson locks up a key part of their passing attack, but with Jacoby Brissett as this team's QB1 and question marks about the future of this position, it remains to be seen what Mike LaFleur's goal is to round out the offense.

Eyes will be on rookie running back Jeremiyah Love, who will look to justify his hefty draft price for a team that didn't have to invest a premium first-round selection in a running back.

articles.title: Why Kyle Hamilton thinks turnovers could spike in Ravens' new defense
articles.summary: Kyle Hamilton offered a revealing explanation for why the Ravens' defensive overhaul could create more opportunities to take the ball away in 2026.
articles.body:
One of the most common predictions surrounding any defensive philosophy shift is that more sacks and takeaways will follow. Well, that's the hope at least, so why should the Baltimore Ravens be any different? There's a new sheriff in town, head coach Jesse Minter , and one of his deputies can't wait to put the shoulder pads on.

There's a new scheme. There's a new defensive coordinator in Anthony Weaver. There's a new philosophy. The assumption has been easy to make. For an explanation of why Baltimore believes that could happen, one need only speak to all-world safety Kyle Hamilton .

Speaking with reporters this week , Hamilton offered one of the most revealing football explanations to emerge from the Ravens ' locker room since training camp began. Rather than making a broad prediction about forcing turnovers, the star safety pointed to a specific schematic change that could increase opportunities for defenders to attack the football.

When asked about takeaways in the new defense, Hamilton resisted the idea that turnovers can be manufactured. Instead, he went into greater detail with a simple yet complex strategy. Baltimore creates more splash plays by keeping more eyes on the quarterback.

"I think takeaways are very flow of the game. You can't really manufacture takeaways. You kind of have to be [in the right] mindset, and I think we've been emphasizing that a lot. I think in the past we played a lot of man... But you don't really have your eyes on the quarterback as much if that makes sense."

The explanation is certainly revealing. Hamilton noted that Baltimore played a significant amount of man coverage in recent seasons. While effective in many situations, man coverage often requires defenders to focus almost exclusively on their assigned receiver.

That leaves fewer opportunities to read the quarterback's eyes or break aggressively on throws. Under the Ravens' new system, Hamilton suggested defenders could have more chances to see the entire play develop.

"Mixing in some man with some zones and just allowing defensive backs and linebackers and everybody to be more aggressive to that sense, getting your hands on the ball. And, obviously up front, winning rushes and getting [the] ball off the quarterback and everything like that."

That subtle distinction could have a significant impact. The goal is not reckless gambling. Instead, it is creating more opportunities for defenders to anticipate throws, get their hands on passes, and capitalize when quarterbacks make mistakes.

Hamilton pointing to complementary football is also a massive part of the equation. A better pass rush can force hurried decisions, while defenders throughout the secondary can react more quickly when they can see the quarterback.

The Ravens are not promising a dramatic increase in interceptions. Hamilton made it clear that turnovers remain situational and often unpredictable. Still, his explanation offered perhaps the clearest glimpse yet into why Baltimore believes its defensive changes could produce one of the NFL's most valuable commodities.

For months, much of the conversation surrounding Baltimore's defensive overhaul has focused on new terminology, new coaches, and new responsibilities. Hamilton pulled back the curtain on something more tangible. The Ravens believe more eyes on the quarterback can create more opportunities to impact the game.

Whether that translates into more interceptions and takeaways remains to be seen, but the thought process is clear. If Baltimore's defensive reset succeeds, Hamilton may have already explained one of the biggest reasons why.

articles.title: Browns news: Did you know Deshaun Watson is 7-0 vs. Jaguars?
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson’s return to an NFL regular-season field will come against a team he knows very well. The Cleveland Browns quarterback enters Sunday’s Week 1 m...
articles.body:
Deshaun Watson 's return to an NFL regular-season field will come against a team he knows very well.

The Cleveland Browns quarterback enters Sunday's Week 1 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars with an impressive 7-0 career record against them as a starter. Now, Watson will try to make it eight victories in nine meetings overall while making his first regular-season start since 2024. Watson did appear in relief in a loss to the Jaguars in 2017, his rookie season.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Watson won Cleveland's quarterback competition over Shedeur Sanders during training camp, earning the opportunity to lead the Browns into the 2026 season. Now comes the significantly more difficult part: proving he can still perform at a high level when the games count.

Watson believes communication throughout Cleveland's offense will be crucial.

"The entire offensive staff is communicating," Watson said. "We gotta meet in the middle, we gotta be able to trust the game plan, and I gotta go execute that."

That execution will be under the microscope Sunday. Watson hasn't played particularly well during his Browns tenure, throwing 19 touchdowns across 19 appearances while injuries have repeatedly kept him off the field. His history against Jacksonville at least provides an encouraging starting point.

Watson also appears to have a different appreciation for simply being able to play again after his lengthy absence.

"I try and enjoy each moment because I know how fast it can be taken away," Watson said.

Sunday provides his next one. Beating Jacksonville won't erase everything that has happened during Watson's disappointing Cleveland tenure.

But after nearly two years without a regular-season start, improving his career record against the Jaguars to 8-0 would be a pretty good way to begin his latest comeback.
