articles.title: Colts' Daniel Jones ranks ahead of Stroud, Nix in Week 1 QB rankings
articles.summary: Colts quarterback Daniel Jones landed ahead of Texans star C.J. Stroud in CBS Sports' Week 1 NFL quarterback power rankings.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones is zipping into the 2026 season with respect ahead of certain NFL starting QBs.

CBS Sports' Garrett Podell ranked Jones No. 19 among the NFL's 32 starting quarterbacks in his Week 1 QB power rankings, putting him one spot ahead of Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud at No. 20 and two spots in front of Denver Broncos QB Bo Nix at No. 21.

"Daniel Jones profiled like a top 10 quarterback before he suffered some lower body injuries that eventually came back to bite him in the form of a torn Achilles tendon. ... Perhaps he can build upon that in Year 2 in Shane Steichen's offense," Podell wrote.

The veteran set career highs with a 68% completion rate, 238.5 passing yards per game, and 8.1 yards per attempt in 2025. Now back for his second season in Shane Steichen's offense, Jones has an opportunity to build on that production.

Stroud's placement is prominent considering his early-career success. The Texans quarterback has won a playoff game in each of his first four seasons, but CBS Sports pointed to his turnover-filled 2025 postseason as a worry.

Nix threw for 3,931 yards in 2025, but his 6.4 yards per attempt ranked 28th among qualified quarterbacks. CBS Sports also noted that Denver punted 75 times, third-most in the NFL, while questioning whether the Broncos will put more on Nix's plate this season after he returned from a broken ankle suffered in January.

For Jones, surpassing both Stroud and Nix indicates how he's perceived compared to playoff-bound quarterbacks from 2025.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill's Injury Return Timeline Updated by Drew Rosenhaus Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Free-agent wide receiver Tyreek Hill and his representatives are "playing it on the safe side" as he prepares for a possible return to the NFL this season.
articles.body:
Free-agent wide receiver Tyreek Hill and his representatives are "playing it on the safe side" as he prepares for a possible return to the NFL this season.

His agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said Wednesday on The Pat McAfee Show that teams have shown interest in the eight-time Pro Bowler. However, doctors have advised Hill to delay a comeback until at least October.

The 32-year-old was the NFL's most electric pass-catcher at his peak. He led the league in receiving yards (1,799) and touchdown grabs (13) in 2023.

Nobody knows what the state of his game will be when he steps onto the field again, though.

Hill's production fell off dramatically in 2024, and his 2025 campaign ended after four games. He dislocated his left knee and tore his ACL in the same knee.

The veteran wideout has been documenting his recovery. In one video posted online this July, he said he had "no power" in his surgically repaired knee.

He appeared to be moving much better during a workout earlier this month.

Rosenhaus knows how to generate interest — or at least manage the optics — with his clients. It wouldn't be a big surprise if Hill effectively had standing offers with multiple teams, though. He possesses a proven track record, and even a version of Hill that's 80 percent of his old self would make a big impact on almost any offense.

And until he proves otherwise, general managers and coaches can talk themselves into the upside of Hill post-injury.

Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh is very familiar with the New York Jets ahead of Sunday's season opener, and he had a bold prediction for his Week 1 opponents.

Saleh, who served as head coach of the Jets for three-plus seasons from 2021 to 2024, told reporters on Wednesday that he expects New York to have a top-16 offense during the 2026 campaign, something the team hasn't achieved since 2015.

"I fully expect them to be a really, really good offense as the year progresses, and I would not be surprised if this unit finishes in the top half of the league," Saleh said. "It's pretty talented."

Saleh was part of the regime that drafted some of the Jets' top offensive stars, including wide receiver Garrett Wilson, running back Breece Hall and guard Joe Tippmann. His tenure as head coach was hampered by poor quarterback play, as 2021 No. 2 pick Zach Wilson was a major draft bust, and future Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers failed to be the savior after tearing his Achilles four plays into his first game as a Jet.

Second-year Jets head coach Aaron Glenn and general manager Darren Mougey made a concerted effort to create some stability on both sides of the ball, and they made their most important move on offense when they acquired veteran quarterback Geno Smith from the Las Vegas Raiders. Despite a down year in 2025, the former Jets second-round pick is expected to help lift the offense to a respectable level in his second run in New York.

"Geno can still sling it," Saleh said. "When he has time and he can throw the ball and he's got weapons to throw to, he can run a very high-functioning offense."

Both the Jets and Titans are in different stages of their ongoing rebuilds, so neither team is expected to contend for a playoff spot this season. Still, their Week 1 matchup carries some extra juice as Saleh faces his old team and New York's players face their old coach, so it could turn out to be one of the most entertaining games of Sunday's slate.

articles.title: Fernando Mendoza Explains Why 'It Feels Great' to Be Raiders' QB2 Behind Kirk Cousins
articles.summary: Days away from his first NFL game, albeit as a backup, Las Vegas Raiders rookie Fernando Mendoza doesn't mind sitting behind Kirk Cousins right now.
articles.body:
Days away from his first NFL game, albeit as a backup, Las Vegas Raiders rookie Fernando Mendoza doesn't mind sitting behind Kirk Cousins right now.

Appearing on Wednesday's episode of Good Morning America , Mendoza explained "it feels great" to be No. 2 on the depth chart right now because he is "all for whatever the team wants and whatever is best for the team."

Even before the Raiders selected Mendoza with the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL draft, they strongly indicated he would not open the season as their starting quarterback.

Cousins signed a one-year, $20 million deal with the Raiders in April.

One interesting note coming out of the Raiders' final preseason game against the San Francisco 49ers was head coach Klint Kubiak telling reporters that Mendoza needed more reps, but it would be difficult to do because regular-season practices limit how much action backup quarterbacks get.

"He needs another three preseason games, and all those rookies do," Kubiak said. "Now that the season is starting, the practice reps get smaller and that's just life. But us as coaches, we've got to get them ready to play and keep developing."

Mendoza is learning to play an entirely different style of offense compared to what he ran in college at Indiana. He took more under-center snaps in his first two days of rookie minicamp than he did in his entire college career.

Just because Mendoza won't open the season as the Raiders' starter, it would be a huge surprise if he doesn't play at some point. The last quarterback taken No. 1 overall who started fewer than seven games as a rookie was JaMarcus Russell in 2007.

The Raiders having a Week 13 bye does potentially complicate things because that leaves a long time to get Mendoza on the field, but their pre-bye schedule includes matchups with the Los Angeles Chargers, Kansas City Chiefs, New England Patriots, Buffalo Bills, Los Angeles Rams, San Francisco 49ers, Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos that maybe want to be avoided.

Mendoza is the long-term future for the Raiders, with the only question being how long does he have to wait before getting to showcase his ability for the franchise.

For now, though, Mendoza will wait patiently while trying to help Cousins and the Raiders in the early stages of the 2026 season. They will kick things off on Sunday against the Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy's Position on Vikings' Depth Chart With Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz Revealed by HC
articles.summary: After entering the 2025 season as the Minnesota Vikings' starting quarterback, J.J. McCarthy received a major demotion ahead of the beginning of the 2026 campaign.
articles.body:
After entering the 2025 season as the Minnesota Vikings' starting quarterback, J.J. McCarthy received a major demotion ahead of the beginning of the 2026 campaign.

Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell announced on Wednesday that veteran quarterback Carson Wentz will serve as the backup behind starting signal-caller Kyler Murray in Sunday's season opener against the Green Bay Packers, relegating McCarthy to the team's third-string quarterback. O'Connell added that Minnesota's backup quarterback will be determined on a week-to-week basis.

The No. 10 pick in 2024, McCarthy was the highest-drafted quarterback in Vikings franchise history. Unfortunately, a torn meniscus in the preseason made him the first quarterback chosen in the first round to miss his entire rookie campaign due to injury in the NFL's modern draft era.

It looked like McCarthy was Minnesota's quarterback of the future when he helped the team overcome an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit in its 2025 season opener against the Chicago Bears, scoring three late touchdowns to spearhead the victory. However, the wheels quickly fell off, as he was limited to 10 games due to ankle and hand injuries and finished with pedestrian numbers of 1,632 passing yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions.

The writing was on the wall that McCarthy's spot on the depth chart wasn't safe when the Vikings signed Murray following his departure from the Arizona Cardinals. The two signal-callers were expected to have a quarterback competition throughout the offseason, but O'Connell named Murray as Minnesota's starting quarterback four days before the team's first preseason game last month.

Now, McCarthy will have to sit and watch as Murray and Wentz get the bulk of the action in preparation for Sunday's game against the Packers. Learning behind a pair of veterans could turn out to be a blessing for the 23-year-old as he tries to bounce back from a disappointing start to his career.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy, a first-round pick in 2024, named Vikings' No. 3 quarterback behind backup Carson Wentz
articles.summary: This time last year, McCarthy had just led Minnesota to a come-from-behind victory over the Chicago Bears in his NFL debut as the presumed Vikings quarterbac...
articles.body:
This time last year, J.J. McCarthy had just led Minnesota to a come-from-behind victory over the Chicago Bears in his NFL debut as the presumed Vikings quarterback of the future.

On Sunday, he won't even be Minnesota's backup. Head coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters on Wednesday that veteran Carson Wentz will serve as the backup to starter Kyler Murray in Minnesota's season opener against the Green Bay Packers . McCarthy will start the season as the No. 3 quarterback.

"This gives us the best chance to win this Sunday," O'Connell said.

O'Connell described the backup situation in Minnesota as "week-to-week." He cited Wentz's NFL experience that includes 99 starts across 10 seasons as playing a role in his decision.

"I'm looking at that right now as a week-to-week thing," O'Connell said of the depth chart behind Murray. "Carson, he's got almost 100 career starts. What he was able to do last year from a standpoint of very limited repetition but being able to apply a career's worth of experience, that's kind of what you need to do as a backup quarterback."

As for McCarthy, O'Connell said that "he's still gonna get a bunch of great work" in practice.

"I'm just really excited to continue to get a chance to work with him and want to make it week to week," O'Connell said. "When we feel like we need to declare something different, we can and we will."

McCarthy's rough 2025 led Vikings to move on from him as starter

The Vikings selected McCarthy with the No. 10 pick in the 2024 NFL Draft after he'd led Michigan to a national championship. He sustained a season-ending meniscus injury before the season started, and Sam Darnold led the Vikings to a 14-3 record as Minnesota's starting quarterback in 2024.

The Vikings let Darnold walk in free agency to the Seattle Seahawks in favor of McCarthy after Darnold struggled down the stretch and in a 27-9 playoff loss to the Los Angeles Rams .

McCarthy was named the starter in 2025. He got off to a shaky start in his Week 1 debut against the Bears on "Monday Night Football," then led the Vikings to 21 fourth-quarter points in a 27-24 Minnesota win.

McCarthy sustained a high-ankle sprain in a Week 2 loss to the Atlanta Falcons and missed five games before returning in Week 9. He struggled with accuracy and failed to complete more than 56% of his passes in four straight games.

McCarthy finished his rookie campaign having completed 57.6% of his passes for 163.2 yards per game with 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions in 10 starts for a Vikings team that missed the playoffs at 9-8. His future as Minnesota's quarterback was in peril, and the Vikings signed Murray in the offseason, virtually ensuring that he had lost his starting job.

Making matters worse in Minnesota was watching Darnold and the Seahawks win the Super Bowl.

Now McCarthy has been relegated to third-string quarterback as the Vikings seek to turn the page on last year's disappointment and return to playoff contention.

articles.title: Dianna Russini is finally ready to tell her side of Mike Vrabel story, but only on this one condition
articles.summary: NFL News: Dianna Russini has remained largely silent since the Mike Vrabel controversy turned her NFL career upside down. Now, that may finally be about to chan.
articles.body: Dianna Russini has remained largely silent since the Mike Vrabel controversy turned her NFL career upside down. Now, that may finally be about to change. According to a new report, the former Athletic NFL insider plans to tell her side of the controversy surrounding New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel, but only after she lands her next job.Dianna Russini has been silent for months. Now her Mike Vrabel story could finally come outRussini, who resigned from The Athletic in April amid an internal investigation into her undisclosed relationship with Vrabel, has reportedly turned down interview requests from major networks, podcasts, and even reality television opportunities. Instead, she appears determined to address the scandal on her own terms.And that raises one major question: What exactly does Dianna Russini plan to say?Page Six reported that she is considering multiple opportunities as she prepares for a return to sports media this NFL season. The report also suggested she could take more than one job. More importantly, a source familiar with the situation said Russini intends to speak publicly about the controversy once she accepts her next position.That could potentially give Russini the first real opportunity to explain her version of events in detail.Will she address the photos? Will she explain the full nature of her relationship with Vrabel? Will she discuss what happened behind the scenes at The Athletic?For now, those questions remain unanswered.What is clear, however, is that Russini's next job may come with something far bigger than a simple NFL media comeback. After months of silence, the woman at the center of one of the NFL's biggest off-field controversies of 2026 may finally be ready to speak. And when she does, the Mike Vrabel story could be far from over.A quick recap of Mike Vrabel and Dianna Russini controversy and where does it stand nowThe controversy began in April when photos emerged showing Russini and Vrabel together at a resort in Arizona. The images sparked widespread speculation about the nature of their relationship, particularly because both Russini and Vrabel are married.More photos later surfaced, including images reportedly showing the two together years before the Arizona trip. Russini pushed back against the speculation, while Vrabel also dismissed suggestions of wrongdoing. But the fallout was severe.The Athletic launched an internal investigation into Russini's relationship with the Patriots coach and whether it created a conflict of interest in her reporting. Russini eventually resigned before the investigation was completed.When The Athletic released the results of its review in September, the outlet concluded that Russini's relationship with Vrabel was in “clear violation” of its standards because it should have been disclosed.However, the investigation also found no clear evidence that Russini used her reporting platform to promote Vrabel or help his teams. The review examined hundreds of stories, videos and podcast appearances and found that the vast majority of her work had nothing to do with Vrabel, the Patriots or his previous teams.Russini responded with a brief statement, saying she stood by all of her reporting. Vrabel, meanwhile, has made it clear that he considers the matter behind him.“We've moved on,” the Patriots coach said when asked about the findings.But Russini apparently isn't ready to close the book just yet.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Seahawks Owner Announces Return of White Throwback Uniforms for 2027 NFL Season
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks' new owners are starting out their tenure by bringing back a fan-favorite uniform.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks' new owners are starting out their tenure by bringing back a fan-favorite uniform.

Seahawks vice chair Neal Khosla said Wednesday the team would be adding a 90s-era throwback look to the uniform lineup during the 2027 season.

The Khosla family shared the news shortly after closing a $9.612 billion deal to purchase the Seahawks from the estate of Paul Allen.

The Seahawks wore white jerseys on the road from 1983 to 2001 before moving to the NFC West ahead of the 2002 season.

The team last unveiled a throwback look in 2023 with the return of the team's royal blue home uniforms from that era.

Seattle is next scheduled to wear the blue throwback look in a Week 6 road matchup during which the Seahawks and Denver Broncos will both wear throwback looks.

The Seahawks are also scheduled to wear the blue throwback look Week 7 against the Kansas City Chiefs and Week 13 against the Dallas Cowboys.

Fans will get a first look at the white throwback look in 2027, according to the Seahawks.com's Ari Horton .

articles.title: Everything Baker Mayfield Said About 'Life-Changing' $165M Buccaneers Contract Extension
articles.summary: Rather than have Baker Mayfield play out the season on an expiring contract, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers were able to sign their starting quarterback to a three-year, $165 million extension on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Rather than have Baker Mayfield play out the season on an expiring contract, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers were able to sign their starting quarterback to a three-year, $165 million extension on Tuesday.

Speaking to reporters about his new deal, Mayfield described it as "life-changing" and praised the Bucs organization for their belief in him leading them now and into the future.

NFL head coaching legend has a Minecraft hobby just as impressive

Mayfield, who had previously set the start of training camp as a deadline to get a new deal done, said the Bucs got in contact with his representatives last week and he wasn't aware of anything until Monday evening.

Despite having a lucrative contract in hand, Mayfield explained it doesn't mean he is a made man now because there are many goals still left for him to accomplish, including trying to win a Super Bowl.

Mayfield was set to become a free agent in the offseason, though the Bucs did have the ability to use the franchise tag if they wanted to keep him.

Instead, the Buccaneers were able to get a deal with Mayfield that ties him to the club through the 2029 season. His $55 million average annual salary is tied with five others for the third-highest among all quarterbacks.

This contract is also the culmination of an incredible rebound for Mayfield. He joined the Bucs on a one-year, $4 million deal as a free agent in March 2023.

Mayfield played well enough to earn a three-year deal the following offseason. He proceeded to have arguably the best season of his career in 2024 with 4,500 yards and 41 touchdowns.

While the 2025 season was a statistical step back for Mayfield with 3,693 yards and 26 touchdowns, his 61.3 QBR ranked 13th and was better than Justin Herbert (60.6), Trevor Lawrence (58.3) and Caleb Williams (58.2).

The Bucs have gone 27-24 in 51 starts with Mayfield over the past three seasons. He led them to NFC South titles in each of his first two years, including a playoff victory over the Philadelphia Eagles in the 2023 Wild Card round.

Things are set up for the Buccaneers to be very good once again in a winnable division. Mayfield has proven he can operate the offense at a high level. There was no reason not to get a deal done, and the two sides were able to figure out a few days before kicking off the 2026 season.

Mayfield, with his fresh new contract in hand, will lead the Bucs when they take on the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on Sunday.

articles.title: Malik Nabers' Updated Injury Status, Fantasy Outlook for Giants vs. Cowboys Week 1
articles.summary: New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers, who is working his back from a torn ACL and full meniscus repairfollowing injuries suffered last September, is on track to play Sunday evening when Big Blue opens its season at home against the Dallas Cowboys.
articles.body:
New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers, who is working his back from a torn ACL and full meniscus repairfollowing injuries suffered last September , is on track to play Sunday evening when Big Blue opens its season at home against the Dallas Cowboys.

Head coach John Harbaugh told reporters on Wednesday that Nabers appears "ready to go."

Harbaugh confirmed that Nabers practiced fully Wednesday with the team in pads before adding:

"I think he's ready to go, man. We'll see, though. I mean, it four days until we play. So if he's ready to go, and he feels like he's ready to go, then he'll play. If he's not ready, then he won't play."

With that, there's certainly great optimism that Nabers can have a great season a la his 2024 rookie year, when he caught 109 passes for 1,204 yards and seven touchdowns despite working with three different starting quarterbacks on an offense that finished second-last in the NFL in scoring.

Nabers had 18 catches for 271 yards and two scores in three-plus games in 2025 before he was sidelined for the season.

From a fantasy standpoint, Nabers is ranked 13th among wide receivers and 23rd overall for point-per-reception leagues, per FantasyPros , which used a consensus of 157 experts for its list.

Nabers shouldn't lack for opportunities. He's the clear WR1 on an offense that doesn't have a touch-dominating superstar à la the likes of San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey or Los Angeles Rams wideout Puka Nacua.

If Nabers is healthy, it wouldn't be out of the realm of possibility to see the ex-LSU star command north of 10 targets a game. He averaged 11.33 targets per game during his rookie year.

The No. 2 option in the pass game might be tight end Isaiah Likely, who signed a $40 million contract with the team last offseason and should see plenty of action. However, there isn't a clear WR2, although the likes of Darnell Mooney, rookie Malachi Fields and Giants legend Odell Beckham Jr. should get their looks.

Ultimately, signs point to Nabers getting back in the mix and being used early and often. Simply put, the Giants need him, and if he's practicing fully now, then it could be raring to go on Sunday.

It's easy to feel pessimistic after he suffered a serious knee injury. The Giants may bring him along slowly at first, and he may not get as many snaps. It's also possible Nabers doesn't return to his rookie year form.

The guess here, though, is that we see something more like his 2024 season and that a 100-catch, 1,000-yard season happens again, provided he remains on the field. He could very well be a top-10 WR option this year and a top 15-20 option at worst.

As it stands, Nabers is a clear-cut starting option in all season-long fantasy leagues. There's simply no reason to bench him off the bat. He should be started with confidence.

articles.title: Raiders All-Pro Brock Bowers reportedly had meniscus trim surgery that will sideline him for season opener, maybe longer
articles.summary: Bowers had a meniscus trim procedure on Tuesday and is expected to miss "a game or two," ESPN reported Wednesday.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers underwent meniscus trim surgery and is expected to miss "a game or two," ESPN reported Wednesday .

Per the report, the injury was diagnosed last week, and Bowers had the procedure in Dallas on Tuesday. Raiders beat reporters noticed Wednesday that Bowers was unexpectedly absent from practice shortly before the report of his injury emerged.

The Raiders had not confirmed or addressed Bowers' status at the time of the report.

Bowers will presumably miss Sunday's season opener against the Miami Dolphins and perhaps beyond. The news is a difficult blow for the Raiders and Bowers as he seeks to build on two standout campaigns.

A first-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, Bowers was named first-team All-Pro as a rookie after tallying 112 catches for 1,194 yards and five touchdowns. He was a Pro Bowler in 2025 despite being limited to 12 games due to a PCL sprain and bone bruise in his left knee. It's not clear from Wednesday's report which knee required surgery.

Bowers is a centerpiece of the Raiders' offense and a cornerstone of their future as they seek to rebuild around rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. Mendoza will start his career on the bench behind veteran Kirk Cousins , but whenever he takes over, Bowers projects as his top target and a safety net for the young quarterback.

A knee injury of any kind is concerning, even if Bowers' initial timeline doesn't project to sideline him beyond two weeks. The Raiders are certainly hoping he'll return on the early end of his reported timeline and that the injury won't linger or impact his health and performance throughout the season.

The Raiders will host the Dolphins on Sunday before playing road games against the Los Angeles Chargers and New Orleans Saints in Weeks 2 and 3, respectively.

Fourth-year pro Michael Mayer is second on the Raiders depth chart and will presumably take over the role of primary pass-catching tight end as long as Bowers is out. Mayer tallied a career-high 35 catches for 328 yards and one touchdown in 13 games, including 12 starts in 2025.

articles.title: Brock Bowers Injury Update, Timeline to Return to Raiders After Reported Knee Surgery
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers is likely to miss "a game or two" after having a meniscus trim procedure on Tuesday, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers is likely to miss "a game or two" after having a meniscus trim procedure on Tuesday, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Per that report, "Bowers got banged up 'a little in camp' and the injury was diagnosed last week and surgery scheduled."

Knee issues also cost Bowers eight games last season, making Wednesday's news even more of a potential long-term concern. It's also possible that a one- or two-game absence is perhaps somewhat optimistic.

It's a huge loss for a Raiders team that seemed likely to once again be built entirely around Bowers and running back Ashton Jeanty, given the lack of playmakers beyond that pair.

When healthy the 23-year-old Bowers has been fantastic, catching 176 passes for 1,874 yards and 12 touchdowns across 29 career games. He's quickly become one of the most dynamic tight ends in the sport and is a matchup nightmare, though injury concerns are now becoming an unwanted storyline in his burgeoning career.

During his absence, backup tight end Michael Mayer should take on an expanded role, while receivers like Jack Bech, Jaylen Nailor and Tre Tucker will need to step up and provide reliable targets for Kirk Cousins.

But fantasy players, fans and the Raiders alike will be disappointed that Las Vegas' most dynamic offensive weapon is sidelined to start the season, especially if his absence stretches beyond a game or two.

articles.title: NFL odds, betting, storylines: 3 underdogs to back in Week 1
articles.summary: Let's look at three spots where some 'dogs are in position to bark.
articles.body:
In 2021, Christmas came early — very early — for NFL underdog bettors. Not only did a dozen Week 1 underdogs cover the spread that year, nine scored outright upsets.

Since then? Favorites have dominated the scoreboard, winning nearly 70% of the 64 season-opening games (44-19-1). Throw in the betting line, however, and it's a dead heat: 32 favorites and 32 underdogs have covered the Week 1 spread over the past four years.

This is hardly an aberration. In fact, per SportsOddsHistory.com , at least seven underdogs have cashed Week 1 tickets for 18 consecutive seasons.

Will that impressive trend continue in 2026? Put it this way: I'm not betting against it. Here are three NFL underdogs I'm recommending in Week 1.

The Cleveland Browns spent the past several months being, well … the Cleveland Browns.

First, they traded a generational defensive player ( Myles Garrett ). Then they got outscored 65-17 in their first two preseason games (despite being favored in both). Then they handed the starting quarterback job to an oft-injured (and much-maligned) veteran who looked like an undrafted rookie in his final dress rehearsal appearance.

So of course I'm backing the Browns in Week 1.

Look, I know new coach Todd Monken took a lot of heat for naming Deshaun Watson his starting quarterback. But that doesn't mean it was the wrong decision.

Yes, Watson was atrocious against Buffalo in his final preseason game (5-of-12, 36 yards, one interception). But he played with the backups in that contest. The previous week at Chicago , Watson was 11-of-15 for 126 yards.

Simply put, I trust Watson on the road in Week 1 against a solid Jaguars defense more than I do Shedeur Sanders , who last year had one touchdown, four interceptions and a 55 quarterback rating as a visitor.

Another reason to grab the points with the Browns: Despite losing Garrett, they plugged a lot of holes in free agency and the draft. Also, unlike a lot of teams, Cleveland emerged from training camp extremely healthy.

Finally, because so many bettors are down on the Browns, we're dealing with an inflated point spread. Keep in mind, Cleveland opened last season as a five-point underdog at Cincinnati and nearly scored an upset, losing 17-16 but improving to 4-0 ATS since 2021 as a Week 1 underdog.

Also worth noting: Since 2021, Week 1 favorites of six points or more are 10-4-1 on the field but just 4-11 at the wagering window.

If you're laying points in this contest, you're convinced that the Bengals have fixed their horrendous defense and head coach Zac Taylor will have his troops ready to roll.

After ranking 25th in both total defense and scoring defense in 2025, Cincinnati slid to 31st (381 yards per game) and 30th (29 points per game) in both categories last year.

So of course the front office targeted that side of the ball in the offseason, most notably trading for nose tackle Dexter Lawrence II and signing edge rusher Jonathan Allen . But it's reasonable to wonder how much both have left in the tank. Allen is entering his ninth season, while Lawrence — who had a half-sack in 17 games with the Giants last year after recording nine in 2024 — is in his eighth.

The Bengals did use their first two draft picks on edge rusher Cashius Howell and safety Tacario Davis . However, both begin the season as backups. And don't forget that Trey Hendrickson , who had 61 sacks in five seasons with Cincinnati, is now in Baltimore .

Another reason to be leery of the Bengals: Under Taylor, they are 2-5 SU and ATS in season openers — and the wins were hardly convincing (27-24 over Minnesota in 2021; 17-16 over Cleveland last year).

Since Joe Burrow 's rookie season in 2020, the Bengals have averaged 15 points in Week 1 — and that average has dipped to 12.5 the past four years.

What about the Buccaneers? They've won five straight openers, including three on the road. Baker Mayfield 's touchdown-to-interception ratio in his three Week 1 games with Tampa Bay: 9-0.

It's been exactly two decades since the Bears kicked off a season as road favorites. In 2006, they traveled to Green Bay and pummeled the Packers 26-0 as 3.5-point chalk.

Number of times this decade Chicago has been a road favorite in any week? Three. That's also the number of times in the last dozen years the Bears started a season 1-0.

Obviously, these trends aren't reason enough to fade the Bears at Carolina. (After all, the Panthers' lone Week 1 victory in the last six years came against the Jets.)

Rather, I'm simply noting that Chicago is swimming in unfamiliar waters as a short Week 1 road favorite. And it is doing so against a feisty opponent that went 11-5 ATS as an underdog last season (including a wild-card game) and delivered eight outright upsets.

Am I completely sold on Carolina quarterback Bryce Young ? No. But I am convinced the defense — which was vastly improved last year and added several solid pieces in the offseason — will take another step forward in 2026.

At the same time, I expect the entire Bears operation to take a few steps back. In going 11-6 last season — their first winning campaign in seven years — they were 6-3 in games decided by five points or fewer, including consecutive 25-24 road victories over the Commanders and Raiders .

A huge reason for that success in close games: incredible luck. Chicago recovered two-thirds of all fumbles that hit the turf, leading directly to an NFL-best plus-22 turnover ratio.

Regression is coming for the Bears in 2026. And it's starting in Week 1.

articles.title: 'I don't have anything to prove': Tua Tagovailoa gets a second shot as a starting QB
articles.summary: Tagovailoa has heard from the critics. Now it's finally time for him to rewrite the ugly ending in Miami.
articles.body:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — The moment of truth has arrived for Tua Tagovailoa and the Atlanta Falcons . After an offseason of doubts, questions and what-the-hell-are-they-doing debates, Week 1 is here at last.

They know what's being said about them, these Falcons. They know the national media questions everything about the way the franchise has handled the quarterback position for the last two-plus years:

Signing a just-off-injury Kirk Cousins to a mammoth deal early in 2024

Drafting often-injured Michael Penix Jr. in the first round just a few weeks later

Watching both Cousins and Penix suffer — wait for it — further injury

Signing very-often-injured Tagovailoa to a one-year deal

Pitting Tagovailoa against a still-recovering Penix in a slow-motion race for the starting QB slot

Naming Tagovailoa the starter … "for Week 1."

The Falcons ought to be thankful the Cleveland Browns exist, because as long as that franchise is around, Atlanta won't have the most confounding quarterback room. NFL.com ranks Atlanta's quarterback situation 31st , above only Cleveland. Yahoo Sports' Eric Edholm, meanwhile, has Atlanta on the very bottom edge of the "Work To Do" tier, just above the lowest "Tankers" slot — and that's due to Atlanta's skill players, not the uncertainty at quarterback.

Head coach Kevin Stefanski — another new face around here — has done everything possible all preseason to deflect the spotlight away from Tagovailoa and onto himself and his staff. He waited until six days before kickoff to name Tagovailoa a starter, and has repeatedly stressed tailoring schemes to players, not players to schemes.

"In Week 1, you want to make sure that you execute at a high level, whether it's a quarterback position or otherwise," Stefanski said. "What we have to do as coaches is make sure that our guys have a really good understanding of game plans."

Tagovailoa has the opportunity to take those game plans and rewrite an ugly ending in Miami — and, perhaps, rewrite his entire NFL narrative, too. Capturing the starting job wasn't a given for Tagovailoa, especially with the financial investment the Falcons have made in Penix.

"It's not something that I take for granted," Tagovailoa said on Wednesday, adding that after losing his starting job in Miami, "you start to process everything and think of all the things that you could change … things I could have done better." Asked to elaborate, he continued. "There's a lot of things I think I could have done better. Turned the ball over, could have played better. My decision making … in terms of last year just wasn't good."

Since 2023, when he led the league in passing yardage, Tagovailoa's production has steadily declined, in part because of the repeated concussions and other injuries he suffered the last two seasons. The Dolphins cut ties with him after the 2025 season, taking a massive $99 million dead-cap hit to end the Tagovailoa era. While his bank account is just fine, the move was a broadside on Tagovailoa's ego, and he relied on his faith to get through.

"Outside of being able to feel centered, it also gives me a lot of perspective on life, on what's important in life," he said in August. "And football is just what we do, it's not who we are."

That's healthy from a psychological perspective, but it doesn't do much against Atlanta's Week 1 opponent. In the first step of his journey back in the direction of respectability, Tagovailoa must go over and around TJ Watt , Cam Heyward and the rest of the Pittsburgh Steelers ' defense.

"The expectation I put on myself every time," he said, "is to go out there and score one more point than the opposing team."

The rest of the team and coaching staff, meanwhile, are doing everything possible to make Tagovailoa as comfortable as possible. Atlanta has significant star power both in the backfield and the receiving corps; the question is, and has been for years, how best to take advantage of all that skill.

"He has a lot of talent around him. I think it's going to make him more confident knowing that," Bijan Robinson said Wednesday. "Me and Tua talk all the time on the field — we talk about angles, where to get the ball out, when to get the ball out. … He can give us the ball anywhere on the field and trust us to make a play."

"Working with all the quarterbacks over my career, whether they started or not, the guys are comfortable with certain things, and they're not comfortable with everything," Stefanski said. "Our job as coaches is to find out what in this broad scheme fits your eye, if you will. What are your strengths? What can we lean into in your strengths?"

What exactly are Tagovailoa's strengths now? That's a question that will only be answered on the field starting Sunday. In the preseason, he completed 10 of 13 passes for 117 yards, the longest going for 37, and no touchdowns or interceptions. He's never had the most powerful arm in the league, but he'll have a talented receiving corps around him — and, of course, Robinson, who's a one-man security blanket.

"Any quarterback, whether it's your first or your hundredth start, likes a good run game," Stefanski said. "It's our job as coaches to put together a balanced game plan because you never know what the game is going to call for."

"How I'm taking it is, I got to go with this day-to-day, and [coaches' decisions are] out of my control," Tagovailoa said. "What I can control is how I prepare, how I go out there, how I play, how I perform, and that's all I can do."

Second chances may be rare in the real world, but they're a fact of life in the NFL, particularly for quarterbacks. In a league where the number of available positions exceeds the number of QB1-level starters, there's always an opportunity for former starters to reclaim their old title … at least once.

For Tagovailoa, this represents a chance to defy his doubters in the most effective way possible. In Atlanta, Tagovailoa now has a chance to silence critics, force analysts to reconsider him, and just maybe move up out of that 31st-out-of-32 slot. He's not framing this challenge that way, but it's there nonetheless.

"I don't have anything to prove to anyone outside," he declared, "but it's proof to my own self that I can continue to play at a high level."

He'll get at least one more start to do exactly that, beginning Sunday in Pittsburgh.

articles.title: Writer makes bold prediction regarding Vikings QB Kyler Murray
articles.summary: Kyler Murray could be a top-12 quarterback in a key metric this season.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings expect Kyler Murray to spark an offensive resurgence after a hit in 2025. With the revolving door of J.J. McCarthy, Carson Wentz, and Max Brosmer, the Vikings ranked 29th in passing offense. Over Kevin O'Connell's previous three seasons as head coach, Minnesota had never ranked worse than 7th in the metric.

That's why there is optimism with Murray. He's played only one full season in the past four years, and he wasn't surrounded by the best roster or coaching staff in Arizona. Not only does he now have O'Connell in his ear, but Murray now has Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and Jauan Jennings, among others, at his disposal. And a renewed emphasis on the running game could also take some pressure off Murray.

ESPN's Seth Walder is optimistic that Murray can not only get his career back on track, but also be a top-12 quarterback in an advanced metric.

"Murray will finish in the top 12 in QBR," Walder wrote over the weekend . "It doesn't feel like that should be that bold of a prediction, considering he did that just two years ago. But considering he was cut by the Cardinals (who need a quarterback) this offseason, that would be a very nice turnaround for the former No. 1 pick. I'm buying him with O'Connell and Jefferson."

QBR is ESPN's metric for evaluating overall quarterback performance, accounting for factors such as passing, rushing, turnovers, game situation, and play difficulty. No Vikings quarterback qualified in last year's top 28 QBR rankings, and Murray, limited to five games, was left off the list, too.

But with a full bill of health and tons of supporting talent, Murray has a chance to climb up the list once again. If he does so, Minnesota could return to the playoffs in 2026.

articles.title: Patriots X-factors against the Seahawks in NFL Week 1
articles.summary: Keys to a Patriots win over the Seahawks on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
Since the final whistle was blown on their 2025 season, the New England Patriots made a commitment to become more competitive against the best teams in the NFL. Well, as fate (or rather the league's schedule makers) would have it, the club of head coach. Mike Vrabel will get a golden opportunity to prove where it stands right in Week 1: on Wednesday night, the team that defeated the Patriots in the Super Bowl will host them on their home turf.

The Seattle Seahawks have undergone some personnel changes both on and off the field this offseason, but all in all are still one of the top teams in football. For the Patriots to leave Lumen Field victoriously, they will have to be on top of their game from quarterback Drake Maye down to the practice squad elevations .

If they are, the contest on Wednesday night should be more competitive. That is especially true if New England manages to out-perform the home team in some critical areas.

With that said, here are our X-factors for Patriots vs. Seahawks from an offensive, defensive and special teams perspective.

There are a lot of reasons why New England's offense was unable to get off the ground in the Super Bowl, but a big one was the pressure Drake Maye found himself under. Capable of bringing the heat with only four players, Seattle sacked, hit or hurried the MVP runner-up on 43.4% of his dropbacks in that game — a number that created a trickle-down effect on the rest of the unit and prompted Maye to go too much into "hero ball" mode for his and his team's own good.

The solution to that is simple: keep Maye clean. Of course, that is easier said than done against a defensive line that gave New England all sorts of fits in the Super Bowl.

The Patriots reacted accordingly in the offseason, moving Jared Wilson back into his natural spot at center and bringing in Alijah Vera-Tucker to shore up a left guard spot that was a definitive weakness with Wilson lining up there. That change, plus Will Campbell 's development from both a physical and technical perspective will be key for the Patriots on Wednesday.

If the Seahawks can continue to create pressure with just four players up front and keep dropping seven into coverage, Maye and company will be in for another tough day at the office. If the O-line wins its battles more consistently, though, everything else could fall into place: the other signings made in the spring — namely A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs — do have the ability to give a Seattle secondary fits that is facing some questions at safety. And if Maye isn't forced into playmaker mode, the turnovers that made a major difference seven months ago might also become a thing of the past.

For New England, just like it did in the Super Bowl, it all starts up front.

Of course, the team's X-factors on offense go beyond just protecting Drake Maye. In addition, the Patriots need to be smart with and without the ball not to risk any plays that can negatively impact series, get their two-back run game going led by Rhamondre Stevenson and fullback Reggie Gilliam , and going for the mismatches especially in that aforementioned secondary.

The Patriots entered this year's offseason with two major areas of concern, wide receiver and defensive edge. They invested premium capital in both of them, but entering Wednesday there are clear differences in comfortability with those groups. Whereas the wide receiver position is one of the deepest on the roster even after the Kayshon Boutte trade to the Texans , the edge is quite possibly the biggest concern on the team.

Entering Wednesday, the Patriots had four edges on their roster: offseason free agency signing Dre'Mont Jones and second-year man Elijah Ponder as the projected starters, with second-round draft pick Gabe Jacas and seventh-round rookie Quintayvious Hutchins as the rotational backups.

A lack of household names is not the only problem for the Patriots. The group very much had its ups and downs in training camp, including in one area that might turn out to be crucial against the Seahawks: perimeter run defense.

The joint practices with the Indianapolis Colts and Philadelphia Eagles made this painfully clear. The team's runners managed to do quite a bit of damage, in large part due to soft edges opening up space to the outside of the formation. And with New England's top-level linebackers not the fastest either, this can quickly become a problem particularly against a team as well-equipped to take advantage as Seattle.

Sure, reigning Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker is no longer a part of the equation after defecting to Kansas City in free agency, but first-round draft choice Jadarian Price is also a back capable of capitalizing on any issues in that regard. Furthermore, Seattle retained its entire starting offensive line — a group that allowed Walker and the rest of the Seahawks' ball carriers to average 4.3 yards per carry outside the tackles in 2025.

Beyond the run defense, the biggest X-factor for the Patriots will be limiting NFL Offensive Player of the Year Jaxon Smith-Njigba , a job likely falling on recently-extended Christian Gonzalez . In addition, the Patriots need to find a way to challenge Seattle's communication along the interior offensive line and to remain disciplined when blitzing.

The Seahawks are fielding one of the best special teams units in all of football, in large part because of the two return men. Rashid Shaheed is one of the most potent all-around returners in the game, while Tory Horton , who might spell him on kickoffs, no slouch either; both found the end zone running back kicks in 2025.

For the Patriots, the goal has to be clear: limit both whenever they align deep to field kicks and possibly run them back. There are multiple schematic ways to do so — you could just opt not to kick the ball to them, for starters — but when all is said and done it all might just come down to fundamentals. What does this mean? Whenever on the field, New England's coverage personnel needs to bring its A-game to get off blocks and cleanly tackle whoever has the ball between Shaheed and Horton.

Doing so without team captain Brenden Schooler , who remains on the NFI list, will be a challenge. Still, in a contest that very well could come down to the final possession, hidden yards created or given up in the game's third phase could be critical. And All-Pro punt returner Marcus Jones alone won't be able to fix issues by himself if the coverage does not look the part.

articles.title: Packers Salary Cap: Jonnu Smith contract details released
articles.summary: Jonnu Smith can make up to $2 million in 2026, depending on how many games he actually plays.
articles.body:
The contract for new Green Bay Packers tight end Jonnu Smith has finally been released, more than a week after he signed with the team. We previously knew it was a one-year deal, but that's all the information we had.

According to ESPN's Rob Demovsky , Smith received a signing bonus of $350,000 to sign with the team. Smith's game checks (which will fully guarantee this week, as he's a vested veteran) are worth $1.3 million. On top of that, he can also earn $350,000 in per-game roster bonuses.

In total, it's a $2 million deal, if Smith can be on the field for every game this season. Smith's cap charge will also be $2 million, as his roster bonuses are considered "likely to be earned" by the NFL, since he played all 17 games with the Pittsburgh Steelers last year.

For perspective, here are the cash earnings that Smith signed up for after his rookie contract:

He's making significantly less than he ever has as a veteran in the NFL.

Head coach Matt LaFleur believes that Smith can hit the ground running in the regular season, not only because Smith previously played for LaFleur with the Tennessee Titans but also because Smith played for Arthur Smith, a former LaFleur assistant in Tennessee, in 2023 (Falcons) and 2025 (Steelers).

Smith was listed as the second-string tight end, ahead of both Josh Whyle and Mark Redman , on their first depth chart of the regular season .

articles.body:
George Pickens believes that the Dallas Cowboys' wide receiver duo of himself and CeeDee Lamb is better than the Cincinnati Bengals' pairing of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins heading into the 2026 season.

Pickens told reporters that "we definitely feel like we're the (NFL's) best (WR tandem)" on Wednesday.

He also gave praise to Chase and Higgins, but explained that "I definitely think me and CeeDee have made a lot more splash plays."

Pickens and Lamb thrived during their first season together in 2025, with the former recording 93 catches for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns. Lamb hauled in 75 receptions for 1,077 yards and three scores in 14 games.

Their 2,506 combined receiving yards ranked No. 2 among all duos in the NFL, only trailing the Detroit Lions' tandem of Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams.

Meanwhile, Chase caught 125 passes for 1,412 yards and eight scores last season. Higgins reeled in 59 catches for 846 yards and 11 touchdowns.

Pickens and Lamb were the more explosive duo in 2025, averaging 14.9 yards per reception combined. Chase and Higgins averaged 12.3 yards per reception together.

Still, it's worth noting that the Bengals' duo played with three different starting quarterbacks as star passer Joe Burrow missed nine games due to a toe injury . Also of note, Chase and Higgins played major roles in helping the Bengals to Super Bowl LVI and the AFC title game the following season.

As the Cowboys and Bengals attempt to maintain their high-powered offenses in 2026, the league's top receiving duo could become clearer at the end of this season.

articles.title: Tua Says He Doesn't Have 'Anything to Prove to Anyone on the Outside' After Winning Falcons QB Job
articles.summary: Tua Tagovailoa isn't focused on outside noise after winning the Atlanta Falcons' starting quarterback job in training camp.
articles.body:
Tua Tagovailoa isn't focused on outside noise after winning the Atlanta Falcons' starting quarterback job in training camp.

"I don't have anything to prove to anyone on the outside," Tagovailoa said Wednesday, according to Will McFadden of the team's official website.

He explained that he goes out each week to prove something to himself instead, per McFadden.

The Falcons named Tagovailoa as their first-string quarterback over Michael Penix Jr. on Monday.

Penix started nine games for the Falcons last season, but wasn't cleared to fully practice in training camp until Aug. 22 while he recovered from a torn ACL that he suffered in 2025.

He'll be listed as inactive in Week 1 for Atlanta while Cooper Rush will serve as Tagovailoa's backup.

The Falcons signed Tagovailoa as a free agent in March after he started 76 games for the Miami Dolphins from 2020-25.

Despite his experience, he struggled with inconsistency while learning a new offense throughout camp.

Tagovailoa appeared in two preseason games for the Falcons, completing 76.9 percent of his throws for 117 yards without tossing a touchdown or an interception. He also committed two fumbles, losing one of them.

Atlanta's starting offense wasn't able to routinely move the chains with Tagovailoa under center during the preseason, scoring just one touchdown in five total drives.

Still, the Falcons will hope that the 28-year-old can find his rhythm in the pocket during a season-opening clash with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. Kickoff is at 1 p.m. ET.

Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Harbaugh declared with the NFL season upon us that he will "support no cause, foreign or domestic, other than the greatness of the Los Angeles Chargers."

This is probably difficult news for Harbaugh's wife and kids to hear, but they are likely accustomed to it since he's entering his third season with the Chargers. He has also been a head coach for 20 consecutive seasons dating back to 2007.

Perhaps the most notable part from Harbaugh is about the "greatness" of the Chargers, which many seem to agree with going into the season. They are tied for the fifth-best odds to win Super Bowl 61 with the Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens the only AFC clubs ahead of them.

Harbaugh and the Chargers have an opportunity to get off to a strong start with matchups against the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders in their first two games before a marquee showdown with the Bills on Sept. 27.
